#3385. 10 Shows Like 'Minimum Wage' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Spinning off of a popular web series, Netflix's Minimum Wage is currently in the middle of a 28-episode first-season run. If that sounds like a lot of episodes for a show in 2026, keep in mind that they're generally less than 15 minutes each, which is perfect for your overloaded to-watch list—especially when they go down so easily. This cringe workplace mockumentary follows the crew of teenagers running a failing pizza place and making (you guessed it) minimum wage; they're under enormous pressure from their boss (Randall Park) to save the business and their one dumb source of income.

The punchy episodes will leave you plenty of time to explore other streaming shows dealing with the utter ridiculousness of the modern workplace. Here are 10 to get you started.

Workplace comedies usually revolve around white-collar office environments (The Mary Tyler Moore Show, 30 Rock, Parks and Recreation, etc.). Like Minimum Wage, Superstore instead follows the staff of Cloud 9, a generic big-box retailer. The show’s deep bench and diverse cast are largely focused on the jokes, but much of that comedy involves the relatable situation of working a job that demands commitment and a smiley attitude in the face of both entitled customers and obnoxious bosses. It's a different venue and age bracket, but a nutty workplace is a nutty workplace. Stream Superstore on Hulu and Peacock.

We're moving away from the workplace and aging things up a bit, but no worries: the name is a little ironic given that the codependent, co-habitating twenty-somethings of the title are hardly mature. Five friends are cohabiting in the childhood home of Samir (Malik Elassal), and dealing with the uniquely Gen-Z humiliations around dating, work, and even health insurance. Only one member of the group has an actual reasonably good job, while career paths for the others include being a temp, waiter, and a part-time ballet instructor. Stream Adults on Hulu.

This offbeat workplace comedy kicks off with a fabulous premise: Jeong Bok-dong (Kim Byung-chul) was a high-level director in a major corporation until one bad meeting saw him demoted. To president! ...of the company's failing Pegasus Mart offshoot. Bok-dong makes it his mission to get revenge by bankrupting the store, hiring eccentrics to execute eccentric, entirely whackadoo plans and accidentally getting Pegasus noticed by customers, who quickly make it more popular than ever. Think The Producers, but in retail. Stream Pegasus Market on Tubi.

It might sound a little (or a lot) niche, but we’ve seen enough headlines about the working conditions at many video game production houses to understand why a workplace comedy set against such a backdrop would make for a dark and juicy comedy. Charlotte Nicdao and Rob McElhenney are the leads, playing a brilliant workaholic and an unsociable egomaniac, respectively, and the chemistry between them gives the show more than enough spark. There's also a four-episode spin-off called Side Quest. Stream Mythic Quest.

A half-hour comedy-drama with an emphasis on the comedy, Gentefied follows three Mexican-American cousins who have built lives in Los Angeles, only to be faced with a new challenge: the looming gentrification of the neighborhood they helped to build via their family's taco shop. Gentefied has a baked-in sense of place and culture and a lot of heart; the second season is even better than the first. Stream Gentefied on Netflix.

Perhaps there's a bit of counter-programming in this dramedy about a couple of scrappy New York City outsiders, but there's a fundamental goofiness to this show about a couple of nice guys who are great at getting themselves into trouble, and equally good at talking themselves out of it. Bryan Greenberg plays Ben Epstein, a quiet guy with any number of big ideas, while Victor Rasuk plays the outgoing, often shameless Cam Calderon; together they manage a startup clothing business with the benefits of neither money nor experience, amiably hustling their way to success, maybe. Stream How to Make It in America on HBO Max and Netflix.

Debuting at the beginning of the Obama administration before getting a surprise revival just a couple of years ago, Party Down is an acclaimed cult sitcom for the ages—lots of laughs, low ratings, and always worth rediscovering. A group of six (or so) struggling LA actors and writers work as cater waiters for a fancy company, with every episode into a new and wildly absurd situation, even as their aspirations far outstrip their actual lives. Stream Party Down on Prime Video and Netflix.

A legitimate sitcom that just happens to be set in Northern Ireland during the violent Troubles of the 1990s, when clashes between nationalists and unionists frequently resulted in violence. It’s a fascinating contrast, brought to life by a writer and creator (Lisa McGee) who lived it. It’s also laugh-out-loud funny—though it doesn’t make any allowances for audiences unaccustomed to Irish accents, so don’t feel bad if you need subtitles until you get the hang of it. Erin, Orla, Clare, and Michelle are joined by James, the only male student at their Catholic girls' school, dealing with normal growing-up stuff in absurd times. This world is a far cry from that of Minimum Wage, but Lisa McGee's sense of the absurd connects both shows—if the setting is a bit more dramatic, the comedy is just as wonderfully silly. Stream Derry Girls on Netflix.

Not a comedy! But about as good an indication of where we are in the modern global workplace as you're likely to find. Hyuk‑jun is a young guy saddled with debt who signs on for some part-time work at a job agency...at 50x the going rate, no less (should've been a red flag). Each new assignment places him in new and increasingly horrific situations, with increasingly arbitrary-seeming rules. But, hey, in 2026, it's a living. Stream Dead-End Job on Netflix.

It's an office (obviously) and not a pizza joint, but the point here is kinda that white-collar jobs in the 21st century can be at least as soul-killing as working customer service. The Office inherited some of the finer tropes of the workplace comedy (mostly involving tossing together a group of weirdos overly invested in their jobs) while also launching a million mockumentary-style shows, running for nine seasons, and becoming one of the most popular shows of its era. Stream The Office on Peacock.

#3383. Apple Maps could soon factor in how long it takes you to park

On some journeys in busy cities, it feels like it can take you longer to park than it does to drive there in the first place. Code spotted in iOS 27.3 suggests that Apple Maps may soon factor in parking time when it provides journey ETAs.

Separately, Waze has partnered with Garmin to help improve the safety of cyclists by using real-time location tracking to alert nearby drivers …

Currently, the estimated time of arrival shown in Apple Maps only measures how long it will take you to drive to your destination. The door-to-door time can be significantly longer if it’s going to take time to park and then walk from the parking spot to the final destination.

Code sleuth pdfu has spotted a strong indication that Apple is working on the problem.

Apple may be working on parking-aware ETAs.iOS 27.3 adds a TimeToPark flag. When enabled, CoreRoutine uses background location and motion data to measure how long you spent near your destination before parking, and how long you walked afterwards. It saves both metrics per trip,… pic.twitter.com/gwgwtHvbgy

Drivers may not be expecting to find cyclists on some roads, and where there are high speed differentials or limited forward vision that can take drivers by surprise and leave cyclists at risk. Garmin and Waze have announced a partnership intended to mitigate the problem.

When a cyclist using a Garmin bike computer or smartwatch chooses to opt in to sharing their live track location, it will show up for drivers using Waze.

The feature is available on the Garmin Edge and any Garmin smartwatch when used with a compatible smartphone and the Garmin Connect app.

#3382. There’s a Good Reason the NYC Marathon Winners Wore These Watches

Over 60,000 runners crossed the finish line at the New York City Marathon last week. When you think of the elites fighting for a spot on the podium, you might expect to see only the priciest, most feature-packed GPS watches money can buy—historically, this meant the most premium Garmin Forerunners. Looking at the wrists of this year's New York City Marathon podium finishers, though,  you’ll see that Garmin—the name most recreational runners reach for by default—was far from the only brand on the course.

Here are the watches I’ve been able to confirm among the top NYC Marathon finishers:

Men's winner, Andreas Almgren: Coros Pace 4 (sponsored)

Men's runner-up, Yemaneberhan Crippa: Amazfit Cheetah 2 Pro (sponsored)

Women's runner-up, Jessica McClain: Garmin Forerunner 570 (sponsored)

Women's third place, Hellen Obiri: Coros Pace 4 (sponsored)

Nonbinary winner, Ryan Montgomery: Suunto Race 3S (almost certainly sponsored, since this watch was released last month)

An important disclaimer: I haven't spoken with any of these athletes. What follows is my opinion, based on what I know running watches offer the people who wear them.

"Garmin" has long been the default answer to "what running watch should I buy?" It earned that spot with reliable GPS, excellent software, and a huge ecosystem. And on this podium, it's represented by a Forerunner 570—a great watch, but at a price tag most runners would struggle to justify.

Of course, sponsorships muddy the water, since athletes wear what their sponsors put on their wrists. But that's exactly the point: Other brands are investing in elite runners because they believe their products can stand next to Garmin's, and it looks like they’re making the right bet.

It's fair to ask whether Garmin's grip is loosening. The company has increasingly pushed toward the fanciest watches with the most features at higher and higher price points. The Forerunner 570 starts north of $500. Meanwhile, COROS, Amazfit, and others are proving that a perfectly solid, competitive watch doesn't need to cost that much. Is Garmin still the best running watch overall? For ecosystem, polish, and depth of features, it's still a strong contender. But "best" no longer means "the only serious option," and the gap between Garmin and the field is narrower than it has been in years. Sponsored or not, seeing two Coros Pace 4s and an Amazfit Cheetah 2 Pro among the top finishers is worth noting.

You don’t need an expensive watch to be elite—just look at the cheap running watches worn by the men who broke the sub-two-hour barrier at the London Marathon this past spring. Training load scores, recovery metrics, maps, music, and smart notifications are nice, but they're extras. If you're shopping for a watch, spend your money on the basics being done right, and don't feel pressured to pay for features you'll never use. Everything besides your time and pace is icing on the cake.

Whichever brand you choose, focus on these basics in your running watch:

The New York City Marathon podium shows a running-watch market that's a bit more competitive and intriguing than the era of "just buy a Garmin" suggests. Garmin is still excellent, but now we’re seeing proof that Coros, Amazfit, and Suunto are all making watches good enough for the fastest humans on the planet. If they can trust those watches on their biggest days, the rest of us can probably trust them with our Saturday long runs.

#3381. Ring’s wheeled and flying robots will patrol your home

Some people use a whole bunch of fixed cameras to monitor their homes, but Amazon has just announced a more flexible solution through wheeled and flying robots.

Both the $250 Drone Cam and $1,000 Rover Cam can respond to alarms or door and window sensor alerts in order to go check out what’s happening and send live video …

Amazon says they are the first two Ring Robotics products, with more likely to follow. Both are autonomous.

Ring Drone and Ring Rover are both powered by AI Pilot, a custom-built system that uses the devices’ cameras, specialized vision models, on-device sensors, and cloud processing to see, think, and navigate autonomously.

AI Pilot simplifies the customer experience, starting with setup. Simply carry Ring Drone through your space or let Ring Rover autonomously explore, and it turns what it sees into a floor plan. It intelligently identifies rooms and suggests patrol points: spots worth extra attention. This could be a side door, windows, a register, or a long corridor, helping eliminate guesswork while also allowing you to add additional points customized to your space and security preferences.

When a patrol or flight is initiated, AI Pilot plans the most efficient route to get to a preset point based on the map it’s created. From there, it reacts in real time—autonomously navigating around furniture, shelving, and any obstacle it encounters.

You can set either device to patrol on a fixed schedule, as well as activate them manually, but they will also automatically respond to sensor alerts and alarms.

When a Ring camera, sensor, or alarm is triggered, [either device] automatically [moves] to previously set patrol points to investigate […] Continuous person motion detection means Ring Rover can alert you and start recording the moment it detects motion in its view—even when docked.

The Ring Rover Cam will begin shipping on December 16 for $999.99, but you can preorder it today. The Drone Cam starts shipping in late January for $249.99, but there’s no preorder yet.

Just like most other consumer electronics, the price of mid-range phones has increased substantially over the course of the last year. They’re still largely considered "budget," especially when many of the best phones and best foldables easily cost $1,299+.

Mid-range phones quite simply offer the right balance between features and performance. For my next face-off, I’m putting the iPhone 17e, Pixel 10a, and Galaxy A57 to the test to tell you exactly which one’s worth getting if you have $700 to spend.

I’ve personally tested all three of them over the last six months, so I’ll tell you how their cameras perform, how fast they charge, how their batteries hold up, and what software features they offer.

48MP (f/1.7) main, 13MP (f/2.2) ultrawide

50MP (f/1.8) main, 12MP (f/2.2) ultrawide, 5MP (f/2.4) Macro

Awesome Navy, Awesome Gray, Awesome Iceblue

As I said in my review, “the iPhone 17e feels more like what the iPhone 16e should’ve been from the start.” It’s also the most affordable option in Apple’s lineup if you’re looking to spend as little as possible, offering a well-rounded experience that gets the job done.

Just as before, though, Apple’s kept just a single camera on the back — which is unheard of in an era where practically everything has a dual-camera setup. But despite this shortcoming, the iPhone 17e’s 48MP main camera performs brilliantly across challenging lighting conditions. From the sharp details and definition it pulls out, to how it neutralizes hotspots in bright scenes, it doesn’t disappoint. It’s also a master of low light, proving to me it’s the best camera phone of the bunch in terms of raw performance.

Under the hood, it’s easily the powerhouse of this trio. Thanks to Apple’s A19 silicon, the iPhone 17e delivers superior CPU and GPU performance that keeps everyday multitasking snappy and handles demanding, graphically-intensive games far better than its Android counterparts. I appreciate that Apple also made a couple of smart hardware upgrades — like bumping starting storage to a generous 256GB and finally adding MagSafe support.

That said, the iPhone 17e isn’t without a few glaring compromises. Holding onto a 60Hz display feels increasingly dated when 120Hz panels have become standard across the rest of the mid-range market — and the lack of an ultrawide camera means it’s not as suitable for sprawling landscapes and group photos.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

And while iOS 27 brings some much-needed new features, like the ability to create custom passes and use generative AI with its Reframe tool to shift to a new perspective for photos, Siri AI remains functionally inferior compared to Gemini. While the assistant is more proactive with what I’m doing on the phone to offer actionable recommendations — like creating a reminder when someone texts me about an upcoming event — Siri AI lacks the deeper third-party app support that lets it work across more apps.

Worst of all, its recent price hike to $699 (up from its $599 launch price) makes those omissions much harder to overlook.

There’s good and bad with the Pixel 10a. Just like the iPhone 17e, the design makes it look like a generic slab — but at least Google’s made the camera housing completely flush and offers some fun color options. Despite these design tweaks, the phone is by and large similar to its predecessor, the Pixel 9a, including how it packs the same Tensor G4 chip as before.

Its 6.3-inch Actua display is surprisingly sharp and bright, besting its rivals with a peak brightness of 1,896 nits in our lab testing. Even better, it posted the longest battery life of the trio with an average of 15 hours and 16 minutes. Better yet, it also delivers the fastest wired charging times we’ve tested — reaching 64% in 30 minutes.

Where the Pixel 10a truly separates itself, though, is on the software front. Gemini remains leagues ahead of Siri AI and Bixby, especially in its ability to execute complex, multi-step actions across different apps. I’m not simply referring to asking it to check upcoming New York Knicks home games and add them to my calendar — I’m talking about everyday things like ordering Dunkin’ Donuts through DoorDash, all with a simple voice command.

If that’s not enough, the Pixel 10a really widens the software divide with how practically the Pixel desktop mode works when I connect it to an external monitor, turning the phone into a surprisingly capable workstation when I happen to leave my work laptop at home. Even on the photography side, new AI tools like Auto Best Take and Camera Coach help you nail group shots and framing without any heavy lifting.

However, Google’s decision to reuse the same Tensor G4 chip as its predecessor puts it at a major disadvantage in raw CPU and GPU benchmarking compared to the iPhone 17e. And in 2026, having a base storage of 128GB feels stingy. Even though the camera performance is better than most other mid-range phones, I’m disappointed that there's barely any improvement over its predecessor — a tougher pill to swallow now that its $100 price hike has pushed it to $599.

Out of the bunch, the Samsung Galaxy A57 has the most premium look and feel — rivaling its flagship sibling, the Galaxy S26. Not only does it combine the glass-meets-metal build Samsung’s known to give its top-tier models, but it also manages to have an IP68 rating.

If you prefer a phone with a larger screen to see more of what you’re doing or stream your favorite shows while on the go, the Galaxy A57’s massive 6.7-inch Super AMOLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate doesn’t disappoint. It’s way bigger than the 6.1- and 6.3-inch screens of the iPhone 17e and Pixel 10a, respectively.

Another notable feature is how it’s the only phone in this trio to pack a triple-camera system on the back, pairing a 50MP main sensor with a 12MP ultrawide and a 5MP macro lens. While that dedicated macro shooter feels more like a forced addition just to give it the upper hand, having three distinct lenses nonetheless gives you extra shooting versatility that neither the iPhone 17e nor the Pixel 10a can match.

Throw in some S26-level Galaxy AI features — like access to object eraser and a voice transcription tool — and it has a robust toolset to help save you time. I also love how it caters to power users like myself, with the ability to run two apps side by side, which neither the iPhone 17e nor the Pixel 10a can do.

Where the Galaxy A57 stumbles, though, is under the hood. Powered by Samsung’s Exynos 1680 chip, it posted the lowest performance scores of the bunch in our testing, lagging behind both the Pixel 10a and especially the iPhone 17e. Worse yet, it doesn’t even have the luxury of wireless charging — a glaring omission, in my opinion, now that its $50 price hike has pushed the cost up to $599.

3DMark Wild Life Original Unlimited (score/fps)

If there’s one I’d buy with my own money, it has to be the Pixel 10a — with the iPhone 17e not too far behind it. That’s because Google’s mid-range phone checks off more of the boxes on my list than the other two.

All three phones got price hikes, but the Pixel 10a’s $599 price tag is easier to swallow than the iPhone 17e’s heftier $699 cost. And while the Galaxy A57 matches the Pixel’s price point, its weak processing performance combined with flat camera results aren’t enough to prove to me it offers better value at the same price.

Ultimately, the Google Pixel 10a is the mid-range phone I recommend. I can’t stress enough the value of its software package alone — and backed up by seven years’ worth of major Android and security updates, it’s undeniably the smartest long-term investment you can make in the mid-range market right now.

#3378. This Actively Exploited Chrome Vulnerability Is Putting Your Browser at Risk

If you've seen an uptick in security updates as of late, you're not alone. AI models have become very good at finding new security vulnerabilities throughout 2026. Researchers and hackers alike are increasingly relying on these models in their individual pursuits: Hackers want to find these flaws to exploit them, while researchers want to block hackers from doing so. Microsoft's latest Patch Tuesday update included more than 1,400 patches; meanwhile, Apple's latest security update fixed two iMessage flaws that let both bad actors and innocent parties alike access texts they shouldn't.

Whether you use a Mac or a PC, you probably browse the web with Chrome, or a Chromium-based browser. As it happens, Google's web browsing platform is the latest to receive an important security update—but it's far from the first important Chrome update of the year.

As reported by The Hacker News, Google released a new update for Chrome on Monday that patches nine security flaws. While all vulnerabilities are important to patch, one in particular is more serious than the rest: CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component.

Use-after-free vulnerabilities happen when the system frees up a memory location, but a program tries to access it anyway. It's a glitch in programming, but it offers bad actors an opportunity to break into your system. At worst, it allows arbitrary code execution, or, in other words, gives hackers the ability to run their own code in the app or system.

That's bad enough on the surface, but, unfortunately, Google confirmed that CVE-2026-125350 has an active exploit in the wild. The company is keeping other details close to the vest, but it's dangerous nonetheless. At least someone, somewhere, has used this flaw against a target, which puts all Chrome users (as well as users of Chromium-based browsers) at risk.

What's more, this isn't Chrome's first active exploit of the year—this is its eighth. The company is playing catch-up with hackers looking to target users of its browser, which makes sense, seeing as Chrome is by far the world's most popular browser.

If you're using Chrome on your computer, you'll want to update it as soon as possible. Make sure you're running at least versions 157.0.8103.50/.51 on Mac or PC, or 157.0.8103.50 on Linux. To check, click the three dots in the top-right corner of your Chrome window, then go to More > Help > About Google Chrome.

Other Chromium-based browsers may not have the update yet, but they are affected by this flaw. If you use browsers like Microsoft Edge, Opera, or Brave, keep an eye on your updates to install any of the latest patches.

#3377. Adobe unveils new AI tools for Photoshop, Premiere, and more, with MCP support coming in 2027

Adobe today announced a sweeping set of updates at its annual Adobe MAX conference, focused on giving users more ways to automate complex workflows, edit content, and work across its creative apps. Here are the details.

At the Adobe MAX event today, the company unveiled a series of features, many of them AI-powered or AI-assisted, that will begin rolling out across its suite of creative platforms as early as today.

In Photoshop, the new Relight tool offers a way to non-destructively and dynamically add, reposition, and resize light sources in the composition, while Generative Restylelets users** prompt the platform to generate variations of an image’s style and fine-tune the results using adjustable sliders.

Photoshop is also adding a Quick Compare slider to make it easier to track before-and-after results, and is getting several features in the beta app, including, per Adobe:

Following its acquisition of Topaz Labs, Adobe is also introducing two new AI image enhancement models: Wonder 4, which combines upscaling, denoising, deblurring, and sharpening into a single operation, and Image HDR, which converts standard images into HDR with improved brightness and detail.

Adobe Premiere is also getting generative tools that make it easier to prepare raw files for a project, including Enhance Audio, Separate Crosstalk, and Separate Sound Source. Adobe is also adding a Generative Remove tool to Premiere in beta, “bringing you the power to remove unwanted objects, like boom mics and logos or background distractions, directly on your timeline,” says the company.

Premiere is also getting Color Mode, a new color-grading tool starting today, which “supports everything from quick corrections to more advanced grades while keeping your video as the focus.”

Another interesting tool making its way into Premiere is Generative Media Tool. Here’s Adobe:

The Generative Media Tool brings Generate Video, Generate Sound Effects, Generate Soundscape and Generate Music directly into your timeline in Premiere. You can generate missing b-roll, background music or sound for a scene using context from your edit, then keep refining the result in your timeline. You can also choose from Adobe Firefly and models from partners including Google, Kling, Runway and Luma based on the creative needs of your project.

As for iPhone users who rely on Premiere Mobile, Adobe announced that its newly established partnerships with UMG and WMG will bring hundreds of thousands of licensed music tracks to the app (for non-commercial use) starting today, with users able to explore trending songs, discover featured artists, and create videos using artist-inspired templates.

Premiere mobile is also getting agentic tools soon, including Quick Cuts, which generates a first cut based on the user’s prompt and the materials they add, and an AI Assistant, which helps users find the right editing tools and execute tasks based on natural language instructions.

In Lightroom, the company is adding multiple new tools that make it easier to edit or more quickly fix small imperfections. That includes Glow, which “adds soft, cinematic light to your photos,” Blemish Removal for quick skin fine-tuning, Open Eyes in beta, and an improved and expanded Camera Tethering on Desktop and the iPad, with support for more cameras and advanced shooting controls, plus the ability to connect cameras directly to an iPad for live previews and photo editing.

Adobe is adding new brushes, gradients, patterns, and graphic styles to Illustrator, alongside new Blend controls, which “make it easier to develop and refine designs with a persistent control panel and live preview,” per the company.

As for InDesign, a new Co-editing feature, available in beta, streamlines collaborative work, while the new Flex Layout tool dynamically adjusts content based on the canvas size and artwork. InDesign is also getting Check Document and Rewrite that more quickly “help identify common editorial and accessibility issues while you’re still working.”

While it will not launch until 2027, this feature will enable users to connect Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects to the AI tools and agents they already use.

In practice, this will mean connecting Photoshop to ChatGPT and having them work in tandem to adapt an entire campaign based on new artwork you develop and attach to your prompt.

This integration will also account for other connected tools, so the user can ask ChatGPT to make edits, add new files to a Google Drive folder, update the team on Slack, and so on.

Here’s Adobe on the upcoming MCP integration:

Because it runs locally on your computer, your agent works directly in your native project files, and your layers, vectors, bins and sequences stay editable.

The company notes that MCP integrations will enter private beta in early 2027, and users can sign up here to learn more.

According to Adobe, Firefly is getting even better at helping users organize and edit their raw material for tasks such as turning travel clips into a vlog, creating social media campaigns, or assembling videos from storyboards.

The new Firefly Video lets users organize scenes, assemble clips, add captions, and generate transitions and B-roll, while Firefly Design brings illustration, image editing, animation, and 3D tools into a single canvas.

Adobe is also adding Quick Actions for common editing tasks, Firefly Graph for creating reusable workflows, and Firefly Builder (in private beta) for prototyping websites and apps using natural language.

Firefly’s AI Assistant is also getting new capabilities, including Plan Mode, which lets users review and approve an agent’s proposed actions, and Model Selector, which lets them choose which AI model to use.

Adobe is also previewing Always-on agents, which can handle recurring tasks such as organizing assets, checking quality, and preparing content for different platforms in the background, even when users step away.

Adobe is also expanding its Creative Agent across Creative Cloud, with AI Assistants now available in beta in Illustrator, Premiere, InDesign, After Effects, and Frame.io, as well as the Photoshop beta app.

These assistants allow users to execute complex, multi-step tasks using natural language prompts. In Premiere, for example, users can ask the assistant to apply effects to an entire sequence, track subjects across frames, or adjust color and exposure across multiple clips.

To learn more about these and other features announced at Adobe MAX today, stay tuned to the company’s blog.

#3375. Latin Grammys 2026 Winners: The Complete List

On Thursday night, Latin music’s biggest stars took over Las Vegas’ MGM Grand Garden Arena for the Latin Grammys, celebrating the best of 2026.

It’s no surprise that Rosalía made Latin Grammys history when she took home her third Album of the Year award after a night of several wins. Before she opened the ceremony with operatic flair, the Spanish superstar took home four trophies: Best Alternative Album for her showstopping album Lux, Best Pop Song for highlight “La Perla,” and Best Short Form Music Video for “Sauvignon Blanc.”

“The truth is I know I have a lot to learn. I know that I’ve probably made my best work but I know there’s still a lot left to be the best,” Rosalía said in her AOTY acceptance speech. “Thanks, mama, for making me this way. I’m going to bring this Grammy to your house. I don’t know if another one is going to fit in your house, but I’ll bring it to you anyways and see if you make room.You always find a way for anything,” she added.

In another emotional highlight, Karol G took home Best Urban Music Album for her 2025 LP, Tropicoqueta after being award Best Reggaeton Performance before the ceremony. “I’m going to very honest because God willing I’ve been up here a couple of times but this one is special,” the Colombian superstar said in her acceptance speech. “People always hear the end result but making Tropicoqueta meant a lot to me that people can’t even imagine.”

Karol continued: “The most important part is to have an album that I can tour because I feel when I’m singing it, people feel proud to be Latina and to carry their flags with pride. That’s the most beautiful part.” Before she walked off, Karol let out an impassioned yell: “Latina forever!”

Milo J had a big night as well, earning his first Latin Grammys ever and eventually walking home with four awards total. The 20 year-old Argentine musician nabbed Song of the Year for his track “Solifican12” and Best Folk Album for La Vida Era Más Corta.

Argentine duo Ca7riel and Paco Amoroso were early winners of the night, nabbing awards for “Best Electronic Music Performance” and “Best Pop/Rock Song.” With their wins, they helped both Fred Again.. and Sting become first-time Latin Grammy winners. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Before the ceremony, superproducer Edgar Barrera led this year’s nominations with 13 nods. Barrera was recognized in the Producer of the Year category and in major categories like Album of the Year and Song of the Year for his work on albums like Karol G‘s Tropicoqueta and Carín León’s Muda, as well as Becky G and Santana’s powerful anti-ICE collaboration.

Trailing him were some of the biggest names in Latin music. Karol G, Rosalía, Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso and Jorge Drexler were all tied with seven nominations each, picking up nods in major categories.

#3374. High-Protein Packaged Foods May Not Be As Healthy As They Look

Of the three major macronutrients—protein, carbs, and fat—protein has the best reputation, and it’s fairly well deserved. We need significant amounts of protein in our diet, and nothing particularly bad happens if we get too much. Dietary protein helps you build muscle, and if you’re trying to lose weight it helps stop you from losing too much muscle along with the fat. It also helps to make meals feel filling. Great! But.

Once the general public gets the idea that something is good for you, the companies that make packaged food start putting it in everything. Or, they make products where the good-for-you thing features prominently on the label, whether or not there is very much inside. So a lot of packaged food now boasts protein on the label. Here’s what you should ask yourself about those foods:

Take a close look here—sometimes a food will boast of a certain amount of protein per package but the package contains two or three servings. Other times, the protein per serving is correct, and we're supposed to be excited to have, say, 7 grams per serving. That's just not very much—and certainly not worth paying extra or choosing a less-delicious food just for those few added grams.

It’s good to know how much protein you need in your diet. If you’re not gaining or losing weight, and not doing very much exercise, a 150-pound person only needs about 54 grams of protein a day. (I've done the math for various body weights here.) If you’re working out a lot, or if you’re trying to gain or lose weight (yep, either way), that same 150-pound person will need more like 81 to 95 grams of protein per day. More is OK, but not necessary.

So if you’re trying to get 90 grams per day, 30 grams per meal is a reasonable amount to shoot for. Coincidentally, 30 grams is the amount of protein that tends to make a meal feel satisfying. You can do the math to figure out whether a protein-added product is going to be helpful in your day’s diet.

I think this is the most important question about protein-added foods. It’s not hard to get protein in a meal; meats, dairy, tofu, beans, and grains all tend to supply plenty. So what is this protein-added thing you’re considering, and are you eating it instead of a traditional meal?

Here’s an example. If I’m heading straight from the gym to run some errands, and I need something to substitute for a meal—yeah, this isn’t great planning, but sometimes it happens—a protein bar with 20 grams of protein is a step in the right direction. Much better than a candy bar, anyway.

But then there are things like this "protein mix" trail mix: 7 grams of protein with 200 calories. A double serving would be 400 calories and only 14 grams of protein. Hardly a great choice if your goal is just to add to your protein intake for the day.

And then there are the chips that my kid, for a time, couldn't stop eating. He loves Doritos and such; on a whim, we bought him some protein chips (yes, these are a real thing). Are they better for him than the equivalent amount of Doritos? Arguably, sort of yes. But then he started arguing that since they have protein, he should be able to eat them in place of dinner. We nixed that, but admit it: Are you having that same argument with yourself, feeling better about a snack food because it contains extra protein? If so, the marketing is working—you’re feeling good about your supposedly healthy choices, even though you’re just eating a bag of chips.

#3371. Rod Wave Asks Judge to Throw Out Evidence From April 2025 Search

Rod Wave says cops overstepped their bounds when they searched his vehicles back in April 2025 ... claiming they had no justifiable reason to suppose they’d find evidence of a burglary inside them.

The rapper filed court documents asking the judge to throw out any and all evidence obtained from searching his grey GMC Denali, black Rolls-Royce, and gold Mercedes G63.

According to Rod’s lawyers, cops were called because of a burglary -- and had no reason to believe the gun they allegedly saw in the back of the Denali was in any way connected to the burglary.

In fact, his lawyers say one detective even omitted that both Rod and another man told officers at the scene that the Denali arrived after the burglary took place ... which they say further reduced the chance that any evidence of the burglary could be found in the car.

Cops allegedly found three firearms, three magazines, and sixteen bullets ... but Rod’s lawyers want a judge to order that evidence thrown out as so-called "fruit of the poisonous tree" from the unconstitutional search.

As we’ve reported ... Rod was arrested about a month after the alleged burglary took place. He was booked on 14 charges, including aggravated assault involving the use of a firearm.

Police say he and one of his associates got into a verbal argument as they were carrying out items from the residence ... which is when a Glock 20 10mm semi-automatic pistol was pulled and fired.

Rod’s lawyers have vehemently denied the allegations against the rapper ... insisting he’s the victim of a burglary and committed no crimes.

A judge has not yet ruled on Rod's motion.

#3370. Everything You Should Know About Black Friday 2026 Sales: Early Deals, Dates, and Retailers

As is often the case with major sales these days, retailers are increasingly blurring the lines between early deals and the official start of a sale. Black Friday sales appear to be becoming a month-long event, with early deals appearing in the first week of the month. If you haven't been paying attention, major retailers have already put out their plans and even started churning out deals. But you're still in time to make this upcoming Black Friday sale a great one. Here is everything you need to know to prepare you for the big sale.

Black Friday is always the day after Thanksgiving. This year, Black Friday starts at midnight on Nov. 27. Cyber Monday is the Monday following Black Friday, which starts at midnight on Nov. 30.

The major retailers doing sales are the usual: Amazon, Best Buy, Target, Walmart, Home Depot, and many others. Currently, Walmart has publicized its plans already and has early deals available. Best Buy is offering one of the largest Black Friday and Cyber Week sales, with multiple events and early deals. Target has a three-day event. Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Cyber Monday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026.

Black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, use price trackers or refer to guides like our live blog that use price trackers for you, and don’t stress over finding the perfect timing. The “best” deal will always depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers that can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot.

Unlike Spring or Summer sales, Black Friday doesn't focus on specific categories, which means everything is fair game for discounts. In previous years, we've seen tech, tools, fitness equipment, outdoor supplies and furniture, bedding, video games, kitchen appliances, and more. If you'd like to avoid having to do all that work, we always do it for you. Just follow our Black Friday coverage.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Prime Day and Black Friday are the two best times of the year to get the best deals on most purchases. Of course, depending on what you're shopping for, you might find other opportunities throughout the year, but in general, Prime Day and Black Friday have the best sales.

Screens, the remote desktop app for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro, is adding two highly-requested features. Version 5.10 introduces remote Mac audio and automatic desktop resizing through Apple’s High Performance Screen Sharing technology.

The remote desktop can now adjust to your screen when you rotate your iPhone or iPad, change your multitasking layout, or resize a connection window on Mac and Vision Pro. You can also choose a fixed resolution.

#3366. Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

There are many reasons why someone might use a VPN, but most often, it’s to conceal your real geographic location or prevent websites from tracking your online activity. It can also be a way to get around location-based restrictions that stop you from accessing certain websites or platforms.

When you connect to a VPN server in the United States, websites are supposed to detect that your online traffic is originating from the U.S. That way, you can access online platforms that use IP filters to block non-U.S. traffic or circumvent regional censorship when travelling outside the U.S. But if you connect to a VPN server in the United States while you’re vacationing in Mexico, and a website thinks your IP address is from Brazil, that might not solve your problem and may even add unnecessary complications.

If you’ve encountered something similar with your VPN provider, there are several fixes you can try. Depending on why your IP location is being misinterpreted, one of these should help you access the internet from the server location of your choice.

IP geolocation isn’t infallible. Websites rely on third-party IP databases to look up your location based on your current IP address. Maxmind, which has one of the largest such databases in existence, claims that its GeoIP products have a 99.8% accuracy. Lesser-known providers with smaller IP databases may be far less accurate.

Websites can also use more than just your IP address to estimate your location. For example, they can send WebRTC requests to your browser or directly query your device’s GPS. Moreover, VPN providers often have physical servers in one country while their IP addresses are registered to another country, and this discrepancy can also create issues. Let’s take a closer look at each of these problems individually, so you can find the fix that works best for you.

WebRTC is an open-source technology that lets your browser reduce latency when engaged in high-bandwidth tasks like streaming or video calls. Based on the IETF standard RFC 8828, it lets a website choose between your VPN server and your real IP address so it can establish the quickest path to transmit large amounts of data and reduce wait times or buffering.

But the catch with WebRTC is that it exposes both your VPN server and ISP-assigned addresses to websites, which can reveal your real IP location and cause websites to reject your VPN server country. Firefox now comes with built-in protections to prevent WebRTC leaks, while Chrome and Edge support third-party extensions like WebRTC Control that you can use to eliminate these issues. To check if your browser is leaking your real IP address during WebRTC requests, you can use a free tool like BrowserLeaks.

Even when a browser isn’t leaking your real IP address, DNS resolvers may fetch inaccurate location information if their nearest servers are too far from your current location. For example, a user in São Paulo may be geolocated to Chile when using Google Public DNS because that’s where Google’s nearest resolvers are located.

If you toggle on DNS leak protection in your VPN app, this will force websites to use your VPN’s resolver to perform DNS lookups. That often solves the problem, but, again, you can confirm the fix worked through a service like BrowserLeaks or IPLeaks.

Websites rely on IP databases like Maxmind, IP2Location, IPinfo, etc. to look up your exact location, but these databases get outdated quickly and need constant updating. Most of these databases also correct errors on request, but that takes some time. Also, each website has its own rules for how often it queries IP databases for updates.

Even when locations are updated in the actual database, a website may be sitting with outdated information unless it actively has refreshed it recently. MaxMind recommends doing this at least twice a week, but that’s ultimately up to the specific website.

VPN providers often rely on virtual servers that use IP addresses registered in a different region than the server’s physical location. For example, ExpressVPN notes that it serves IP addresses in Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela through servers located physically in Brazil.

While this is usually to help with the lack of local infrastructure or strict surveillance laws in the region, many databases and analytics tools will flag the discrepancy for websites, leading to confusion and inconsistency regarding your actual server location. In these cases, your best bet is to switch your VPN server or use a dedicated IP address by signing up for a paid add-on for your VPN.

Before investing in a specific solution, it’s better to do a thorough lookup to make sure why your IP address is pointing to the wrong location and whether a WebRTC or DNS issue, virtual servers, or something else is the cause. Here’s how I’d go about it, step by step:

We’ll start by recording your baseline IP address, country, city, and ASN. With your VPN disconnected, navigate to IPConfig.co on your browser to grab your default IP details. I like this tool because it’s free and uses echoip to pull your location data straight from Maxmind. If you prefer using Terminal instead of your browser, you can also run curl ifconfig.co/json to grab these details in plain text format.

Now connect your VPN server. Then visit IPConfig.co again to note down the changed details.

Make sure the Country and Timezone fields match your current VPN server location. Also make sure the ASN (organization) field does not list your home ISP.

In case these details do not match your VPN server, run a WebRTC leak test and a DNS leak test using BrowserLeaks. If either of these tests doesn’t return your VPN server’s IP address, you’ve found your culprit.

If both the leak tests come back clean but a specific site still gets your location wrong, the issue is likely originating from an outdated database or virtual server.

There’s no surefire way to solve IP location mismatches for good. But if it happens often enough to disrupt your internet use, you can consider switching to a different VPN server and getting a browser add-on that prevents WebRTC leaks. If that doesn’t work, I’d consider buying a dedicated IP address that isn’t based on a virtual server. While many IP databases like MaxMind or IP2Location also have ways to request a location correction, that takes a while to go through and isn’t worth the effort unless it’s a permanent IP address registered through your ISP.

#3361. Hackers Now Want Your Browser Sessions More Than Your Passwords, but You Can Stop Them

There’s a very organized dark web supply chain that attackers use to trade in stealer logs. Russian Market has effectively replaced Genesis Market as the new storefront for black hat cybercriminals, although much of the market has also shifted to private channels on Telegram.

According to threat analysts at DarkOwl, approximately 180,000 stealer logs were sold on Russian Market in just the first half of 2025. What's more, Russian Market is a well-designed storefront that users can access even without Onion links or the Tor browser. That means anyone could go there and buy a bunch of stealer logs to start attempting account takeovers at scale.

Meanwhile, Flare Research estimates that this isn’t even close to the actual scale of the threat, because 90% of stealer logs now surface privately on Telegram. There, automated chatbots let scammers shop for stealer logs like it’s Amazon, with options to filter by country, app, and account privilege. Logs sell for anywhere between $5 and $500 a piece, depending on the estimated value of the target accounts.

The easiest way to go about this is to take a look through all your active devices and their locations in your account settings on most websites. If you see a device or location you don’t recognize, you are likely the subject of an ongoing breach. However, keep in mind that this may not always be a reliable method if you use iCloud Private Relay or a VPN. Still, it's generally best practice to log out of all active sessions every once in a while and perform a fresh login to invalidate any unauthorized sessions.

Reset the passwords on your email account, enable two-factor authentication for added protection, and sign out of all sessions before doing a fresh login. Your email inbox is the single point of entry for most attacks because that’s where most websites send their verification codes or magic links.

Sign out of all active sessions on every account that you suspect is compromised. This will log out any attackers who are currently on a hijacked browsing session.

Change your passwords on every platform in order of priority. Start with banking websites, cloud storage providers, and password managers first.

Look through each compromised account’s third-party integrations and app permissions. Revoke access if you can’t recognize an app, or it looks suspicious. Also make sure to rotate any API keys that you’re currently using, since those may have been compromised as well.

But while the initiative has already been open-sourced, no other major online provider has begun offering native support for it as of this article. That means DBSC’s security benefits are limited to Google services like Gmail and Docs, Chrome for Windows, and third-party websites that offer single sign-on (SSO) options for your Google account. We might see a wider rollout in the near future, though.

It's not as high tech as the Eight Sleep but it will still help offset any night sweats and it's a cheaper option. A dual cover is also available, for bed sharers.

I've tested the Orion Sleep Sytem and its fast-response water-based cooling blew me away. It's cheaper than the Eight Sleep (especially in this massive sale) with a queen now down from $2,395 to $1,795. #3354. Apple TV launches new sign language accessibility feature

Apple today launched a neat new accessibility feature for the Apple TV streaming service. Users will now have the option to watch with a sign language interpretation for some of Apple’s original movies.

The feature is launching this Friday with the debut of the new film Being Heumann, as well as F1: The Movie. Support for more titles will follow later.

Alongside those two films, Apple said that sign language options will be available for Greyhound and Way of the Warrior Kid later this year, with more to come.

To access the new functionality, you need to be using the Apple TV app on iPhone, iPad or Mac running 27.2 or later. The feature will also be available on some versions of the Apple TV app on other platforms.

By default, the Sign Language controls are hidden. If you want to use the feature, firstly go to the Settings app -> TV app, and enable the Sign Language display.

Then, on eligible titles, a new Sign Language button will appear in the player controls. You can simply toggle to enable, and choose from American Sign Language or British Sign Language modes.

When enabled, a signing interpreter then appears in the corner of the frame, synced with the video playback.

When browsing the catalog, sign language availability will also be shown next to the usual subtitle and audio language information. Users will also be able to search “with ASL” or “with BSL” to find compatible titles.

#3353. Dolly Parton Heals the Soul on Final Recording, ‘Torn,’ a Duet With Bono on U2’s New Album

For those missing Dolly Parton (and there are many), the country great’s final recording may feel like a revelation.

On Friday, U2 released their 16th studio album, Carnaval de Luz, which saves the best for last: “Torn,” a duet between frontman Bono and Parton. The singer, who died in August at age 80, recorded her part in June, and shares writing credits for the song with the band and Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid. ”When she got ill,” Bono told Rolling Stone for U2’s recent cover story, “she got out of her bed to sing this song. And you can hear that. And I can’t even listen to it now.”

The song opens with faint voices in the background over a steady heartbeat and soon, Parton’s distinct vibrato fills every lyric. At first, a story about someone deciding between over two lovers appears to be unfolding, until the chorus with Bono reveals a broader division: “Torn apart these loving hearts that beat and break the same/We share a house divided and the blood that fills our veins/Brothers turn to strangers and sons deny their name.” On a verse, Parton sings, “Nothing hurts a mother more than a family at war.”

Bono initially pursued Parton for a still-in-progress Irish-roots side project and while he played her a few sketches over the phone, he recalled her replying, “That’s a little too Irish.” Bono said she eventually sent a song of her own, titled “Torn.”

While Parton originally wrote it around tale of a woman trying to choose between two men, Bono and McDaid rewrote the lyrics around a mother watching her family split apart. “You name the location,” Bono said when discussing the tensions the song evokes, “but everyone knows what it is … People say in the U.S. now, people are scared to go into Thanksgiving.”

Parton agreed to sing the new version. “She sang her heart out,” said Bono, “and I cannot believe that’s an 80-year-old woman.” Longtime U2 collaborator Daniel Lanois added pedal steel on the track, and Larry Mullen Jr. completed it with a drum part inspired by a Lanois production, Bob Dylan’s “Most of the Time.”  Trending Stories Pink Floyd's Roger Waters Files for Divorce From Fourth Wife Kamilah Chavis After 5 Years of Marriage John Mulaney Has Many Thoughts on the 2026 Rock Hall Inductees — And Picks Next Year’s Class The ‘You Can See Everything’ Interview You’ve Been Waiting For Latin Grammys 2026 Winners: The Complete List

Parton approved the final mix and “loved it,” said the album’s producer, Garret “Jacknife” Lee. He added, “She was so proud of her vocal and the recording.”

The Edge told Rolling Stone that he sees Parton embodying “the radical center, which is becoming like a no-man’s-land right now … We have aspirations in that area ourselves, but things have got so polarized, it’s very, very hard to not be taken down by both sides … But she managed to get accepted by both sides and beloved by everyone. That’s an amazing thing. And she did it, as Bono pointed out today, with humor. Humor was her secret weapon. And no tyrant has a defense against humor, turns out.”

#3350. iPadOS 27.3 adds new iPad setting I instantly turned on

iPadOS 27.3 is currently available in beta, and it introduces a new iPad setting for app windowing that I instantly turned on. Here are the details.

I use the iPad Pro as my primary computer, and for the most part have found Apple’s software changes in iPadOS 26 and 27 to be great upgrades.

But with the powerful new windowing capabilities, there have definitely been some quirks that need refining. One of them involves resizing windows with the traffic light controls in the top-left corner.

For example, in iPadOS 27 the controls move locations and even disappear depending on the size of the window. It can be pretty frustrating.

I need to just get better about learning keyboard shortcuts for window controls. But in the meantime, iPadOS 27.3 adds a new optional setting that I instantly turned on and have been loving.

Inside Settings ⇾ Multitasking & Gestures, if you have ‘Windowed Apps’ enabled you’ll see a new option below it: ‘Double-tap Top of Window to Zoom’

If you use your iPad mostly with touch input, or simply haven’t used keyboard shortcuts enough to remember them, this new setting is a great way to quickly resize windows.

When the setting is enabled, two taps (or a double-click with the trackpad) will zoom the window to take up the full screen. Then you can double-tap again to revert it to its previous size.

I generally keep my app windows in specific size setups, but regularly find myself wanting to go fullscreen temporarily. The new setting provides a convenient way to do that quickly without needing the traffic light controls or my keyboard, and is a welcome refinement to iPadOS windowing.

Will you enable this new iPadOS 27.3 setting? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.

As it turn outs, 'pressure' is a good thing when it comes to sleeping through the night

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Picture the scene: you're mentally drained but can't fall asleep. Worse still, after you eventually do nod off, you find yourself wide awake at 3 a.m., staring at the ceiling, unable to go back to sleep.

That was my reality for months until a sleep doctor explained that the coping mechanisms I was using to get through my days were likely contributing to my 3 a.m. wake-ups.Here Dr. Ana Casas, a longevity and internal medicine specialist, and Dr. Shelby Harris, a Board-Certified Clinical Psychologist at Better Sleep, explain what sleep pressure is and why it's crucial for dropping off and sleeping through the night.

"Think of sleep pressure as your brain’s natural hunger for sleep," explains Dr. Casas, who co-authored the book Take Back Your Sleep: The Science-Based Strategy for Deep Sleep, Brain Longevity, and Peak Performance.

"Just as your body becomes hungrier the longer you go without food, your brain becomes hungrier for sleep the longer you stay awake."

"This is one of the two primary forces that regulate sleep, alongside our circadian rhythm, or internal body clock," adds Dr. Harris.

"When sleep pressure is sufficiently high and aligned with our natural circadian rhythm, we are more likely to fall asleep easily, move through the appropriate stages of sleep, and stay asleep throughout the night."

Healthy adults clocking up between seven and nine hours of overall sleep should be spending 45 to 90 minutes in deep sleep, experts recommend. Deep sleep is hugely important for our overall energy levels and stress management. Here are the common mistakes experts said were robbing me of sleep pressure and, as a result, the amount of time I was spending in deep sleep:

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

One of the mistakes I've made when it comes to building sleep pressure is using mental exhaustion as an excuse not to incorporate movement into my day. After all, I feel mentally drained — why do I still need to exercise? "A demanding workday can leave you feeling exhausted, but prolonged periods of sitting and limited physical activity may mean you haven't built as much sleep drive as you think," explains Dr. Harris, who notes that incorporating movement into the day supports healthy sleep patterns. "This doesn't mean you need an intense workout every day," says the sleep doctor. "Walking, taking movement breaks between meetings, getting outside in natural daylight, or doing some light exercise can all make a difference. The goal is to give your body enough activity and daytime stimulation to support restorative sleep at night."As well as helping build sleep pressure, a study by the University of Texas indicates that getting as little as 10 minutes of moderate to vigorous exercise per day could help you get more deep sleep.

When you've had a rough night's sleep, you might mistake caffeine as your friend, helping you to power through the day. I know I have. However, caffeine has a half life. That means that half the amount of caffeine you have consumed will still be swirling around in your system between 3-7 hours later, depending on your tolerance to it.What does that have to do with sleep pressure? "Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors in the brain, temporarily masking our natural sleep pressure even though adenosine continues to build up," explains Dr. Casas.

Sleeping in on the weekend or going to bed early is a common go-to method of catching up on lost sleep. However, this can make it much harder to fall asleep later that night. "One of the biggest mistakes is spending too much time in bed, particularly when people try to compensate for a poor night's sleep by going to bed significantly earlier or sleeping in later," says Dr. Harris. "This can reduce the amount of time spent awake and prevent sufficient sleep pressure from building."Napping or falling asleep in front of the TV (guilty) has a similar effect. Sticking to a consistent sleep schedule is your best bet for allowing adequate sleep pressure to build. If you must nap, Dr. Harris recommends keeping them "relatively short and earlier in the day so they don't interfere with nighttime sleep pressure."

"Ultimately, healthy sleep isn't just about what you do at bedtime," concludes Dr. Harris. "It's about building the right conditions throughout the day so your body is naturally ready for sleep when night comes." These are her expert tips to increasing your sleep pressure so you can fall asleep quicker and stay asleep all night.

"If we haven't built up enough sleep pressure during the day, we may find it harder to fall asleep or experience more fragmented sleep," explains Dr. Harris, who notes that the first half of the night is when we tend to clock up the majority of our overall deep sleep. This is thanks to a healthy bank of sleep pressure that's been building throughout the day, lulling us into deeper, slow-wave sleep. When we're in a sleep pressure deficit, it takes us longer to fall asleep and can lead to waking up at night — specifically at 3 a.m.

"As the night progresses, that pressure naturally dissipates, and our sleep architecture shifts toward lighter stages of sleep and longer periods of REM sleep," explains Dr. Harris. "Around 3 a.m., depending on when someone goes to bed, they may be moving through these lighter sleep stages, making them more susceptible to waking from environmental disruptions, stress, or changes in body temperature," continues the sleep doctor. "If someone hasn't built up sufficient sleep pressure during the day, this transition can make it harder to maintain consolidated sleep," says Dr. Harris, who notes that insufficient sleep pressure isn't the only cause of waking up at night. "It's important to remember that 3 a.m. wake-ups aren't always caused by sleep pressure alone – circadian rhythm disruptions, alcohol, stress, and hormonal changes can also play a role."

#3346. Aura's Second E-Ink Picture Frame Is Much Improved, and Much Cheaper

Last year, Aura released the Aura Ink, its first digital photo frame using an e-ink display rather than the LCD screens common to the other devices that made them the major player in the market (Aura customers have already uploaded more than one billion photos this year alone). When I reviewed the original 13-inch Aura Ink last year, I recommended it, with a few major reservations. Today, Aura announced its second-generation 10-inch Ink frame, and while I wouldn't exactly say they've solved every one of my issues, the new device is significantly improved—and much cheaper.

Most digital photo frames will remind you of an iPad with a decorative border around it. They're great for displaying hundreds of your photos with vibrant color, but not everyone loves the look, or the fact that these frames always need to be plugged in. An e-ink frame, on the other hand, uses a variant of the sort of low-power screen you'd find in a Kindle Colorsoft—less bright, but more paperlike, and much closer to the look of a traditionally printed photo.The Aura Ink is a great choice if you want a digital frame that looks more like a "real" photo and doesn't need to be plugged in and doesn't light up like a tablet (though it does have a light, it's really to make up for the fact that color e-ink screens don't reflect light very well, and thus can make your pictures look way too dark without an additional boost). You'll still get all the benefits of an LCD frame like the Aura Aspen, including the ability to load photos from anywhere using the versatile Aura app (you can now even text them directly to the frame), but you'll only need to charge it once every few months.

Now for the downsides: Where most digital frames allow you to flick between photos with a swipe, the Aura Ink is much more sluggish—switching from one photo to another takes about 45 seconds. While an LCD can match the colors in your photo exactly, e-ink uses a "dithering algorithm" to blend tiny pixels together to create the illusion of different hues ("millions" of them, according to Aura). In practice, this means up close, your pictures will look rather grainy, and the colors won't be nearly as bright as what you see on your phone screen.

All of that said, the Aura Ink is a great product, provided you know what you're buying, and the new 10-inch model offers some big upgrades over the 13-inch original released in 2025:

Resolution has been bumped up from 150 ppi to 200 ppi, so your images look more detailed and less grainy. (Though the difference is hard to capture in a photo, I can definitely see the improvement when comparing them side-by-side.)

Instead of the six base colors available on the older frame, the 10-inch Aura Ink blends nine different hues to approximate the colors in your images, offering greater color accuracy and improved contrast.

The transition effect when you move between photos has been updated to look more intentional—like waves of color moving across the screen versus a series of increasingly intense flashes.

It's a heck of a lot cheaper: $349, versus $499 for the 13-inch model—though that's still significantly pricier than Aura's most popular offering, the 10.1-inch Aura Carver, which starts around $200 less.

I write a lot about e-ink devices, from e-readers to tablets, and my common refrain, especially with color devices, is that they're great at what they do, but you should understand what they do before you plunk down your money. The Aura Ink will never look as bright and colorful as an LCD frame, and if you want a frame that can switch between images every few minutes or even play video, you'll need to look elsewhere (to maximize battery life, Aura recommends swapping photos on the Aura Ink no more than 12 times per day).

But if you want to display photos that look more like the ones that hung on the walls of your childhood home, in a frame that doesn't need to be plugged in all the time, you'll probably dig it, provided you can stomach the $350 price tag.

Keeping your calf muscles strong can benefit your body in many ways

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I didn't know until quite recently that your calves are known as the "second heart" because they help pump deoxygenated blood back up the body. Not only that, but they also play a role in absorbing force during lower-body movement and provide stability to your lower limbs.

I'm not great at sitting still, so during my working days at my desk, I am known to have a quick wander to quell restless legs, and recently I learned about an exercise called a soleus push-up.

I've been performing maximum reps every hour while seated during my workday, and I've noticed a few things so far. Read on to find out more.

A soleus push-up (SPU) is a seated calf raise exercise that targets the deeper calf, or soleus muscles.

Collectively, the soleus and gastrocnemius muscles form your calves and are referred to as a secondary heart. These muscles help pump blood toward the heart, squeezing the veins with contractions so oxygen-depleted blood travels up the body rather than pooling in your lower limbs.

To keep circulation going, being as active as possible helps, including walking, running, or cycling. You may also find elevating your legs at times can be useful, especially after prolonged sitting. But if you don't fancy swinging your legs up onto your desk in the office, seated calf raises or soleus push-ups can help.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

But before we get into what happened when I tried it every hour, every day, for one week during work, there's a study I think you should know about. Published in the Journal of Biomechanics, the research found that people with chronic heart failure had smaller calf muscles (namely, the deeper soleus muscle that helps us walk and stand) than people deemed "healthy" with "functional hearts."

Performing these muscular contractions seated can be useful for people who have desk jobs or want to limit fatigue and blood pressure issues.

Here's what happened when I tried the exercise every day.

Research found that people with chronic heart failure had smaller calf muscles (namely, the powerful soleus muscle that helps us walk and stand) than people deemed "healthy" with "functional hearts."

I have very mobile, clicky joints, and my ankles get both noisy and stiff if I don't move often enough, so adding as many reps as I could for 60 seconds per hour during my workday really helped.

I set eight alarms, one for every hour, and timed myself for 60 seconds, performing reps at my desk while still working.

When I got up to move around, particularly later in the week, I found my ankles felt more mobile and warmed up, and my calves felt less stiff. I recommend learning how to do calf raises, as well as trying some ankle mobility exercises and lower-body stretches alongside this move to ramp things up further.

Because the movement is driven from the lower limbs while seated, it's extremely accessible and low-impact, meaning most people don't even need to stop working while performing the soleus push-up. That also means you can go for high rep ranges while sitting at a desk.

The soleus muscles thrive on sustained periods of movement, so this makes it an ideal exercise to repeat during the week while keeping those muscle contractions going during seated periods.

I added ankle weights to increase the intensity, and this is safe to do because there's no impact. I found it worked my muscles harder and, after stopping 60 seconds later, I felt like I'd been walking up a set of stairs. Add weights just above your knees for even more resistance.

Marc Hamilton pioneered the soleus push-up at the University of Houston and published findings in the journal iScience, saying the exercise provides "optimal activation" and "elevates muscle metabolism for hours, even while sitting."

He adds that the exercise helps sustain an "elevated local oxidative metabolism" which can improve blood glucose regulation by helping clear blood glucose from the bloodstream. Oxidative metabolism refers to a process where oxygen helps burn blood glucose or fats, depending on the energy needs of your working muscles.

“No one ever investigated how to use it to optimize our health, until now,” says Hamilton. “When activated correctly, the soleus muscle can raise local oxidative metabolism to high levels for hours, not just minutes, and does so by using a different fuel mixture.”

Of course, without a carefully controlled lab setting, I couldn't tell you if this made a difference for me or not.

I can be subject to swollen ankles and a little numbness in certain positions, a condition my musculoskeletal doctor hasn't been able to pinpoint just yet, so I was intrigued that soleus push-ups could boost circulation.

A week later, although not life-changing, I have noticed less swelling and numbness while sitting. This makes sense, as your soleus muscle helps pump blood toward the heart.

Plus, as we age, calf strength can decline, which can have a knock-on impact on gait and balance during movement. By maintaining strong, healthy calves, I know I'm reducing the workload on my joints, namely my ankles and knees, which should benefit me heading into my later years.

Keeping them strong can make everyday activities feel easier, too, while also improving balance, ankle stability and overall lower-limb function.

So, according to science, these muscles protect your heart, aid circulation, help produce movement, and impact gait and balance. What more reason do you need to give this exercise a try the next time you're seated?

#3341. New Apple TV 4K remote’s best feature requires a newer iPhone model

A new Apple TV 4K releases this Friday (pre-order here), with an upgraded Siri Remote. But the new remote’s best feature might not work on your iPhone.

If you’re interested in the new Apple TV 4K launching this week, or perhaps you just want to buy the upgraded Siri Remote separately (available here), there’s a key limitation you should know.

Precision Finding on the new Siri Remote requires an iPhone 17 or newer.

The most common problem with the current Siri Remote is that it’s easy to lose. And once you lose it, Apple doesn’t offer many options for finding it. But that’s changing with the 4th gen Siri Remote.

You can use the new Siri Remote with any previous Apple TV 4K or Apple TV HD model. And if you do, you’ll benefit from the remote’s new built-in speaker that can be triggered from the Find My app.

Joining the new speaker, the other main change with this latest Siri Remote is Precision Finding. If you’ve ever used the Find My app to track down a lost AirTag, you’ll probably be familiar with the feature.

Precision Finding lets you get step-by-step, guided directions that take you directly to the lost Siri Remote. It’s a huge upgrade from the old tool for finding the remote—which mostly just told you that it’s in your house somewhere.

But Precision Finding relies on the Bluetooth 6 support found in iPhone 17 and 17 Pro models (not iPhone 17e), iPhone Air, iPhone Duo, and iPhone 18 Pro models.

So if you don’t have one of those iPhones, you’ll still benefit from the built-in speaker that lets you play a sound to find the lost remote, but Precision Finding won’t be available.

You can buy the new Siri Remote for $59 on Amazon.

Will this limitation impact your Siri Remote purchase decision? Let us know in the comments.
