The holiday movie season is almost here, and there’s plenty to look forward to if you’re planning a trip to the theater. November and December 2026 are bringing some huge releases to the big screen, including the return of the Avengers in “Doomsday,” another trip to Arrakis in “Dune” and a new chapter in the “Hunger Games” franchise.

There’s also a festive horror sequel, a new adventure that brings a beloved video game to life outside its console, and a chilling medieval werewolf horror from “The Witch” director Robert Eggers. Clearly, the coming weeks have plenty to offer. I’ve rounded up seven of the biggest movies hitting theaters this holiday season, so you can start planning your next cinema trip. Here’s what deserves a spot on your watchlist.

“The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” is easily one of the biggest movie releases to look forward to this month, thanks to the franchise’s huge fanbase and enduring popularity. It marks the fifth film directed by Francis Lawrence in the dystopian series, bringing him back together with the creative team behind its distinctive cinematic style. Lionsgate moved quickly to bring Suzanne Collins’ latest novel to the big screen, announcing the film adaptation alongside the book in 2024. The novel went on to become a major bestseller.

Set 24 years before the events of the original film, “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” follows 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) as he prepares for the 50th annual Hunger Games. Living in District 12, Haymitch’s life changes when his name is selected during the Reaping, forcing him to leave behind his family and girlfriend, Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak). This year’s competition, known as the Second Quarter Quell, doubles the number of tributes sent into the arena. Alongside fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), Haymitch must fight to survive.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" hits theaters on Nov. 20

“The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is an intriguing follow-up for fans of “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” with Quentin Tarantino returning to write the story and David Fincher taking over directing duties. This time, the setting shifts away from the sun-soaked nostalgia of 1960s Hollywood towards a much darker 1970s crime backdrop. Fincher’s visual style should give the film a distinctly different feel with a much grittier atmosphere. It’s also a notable release for Netflix, which is giving the movie an IMAX-first theatrical run before it arrives on the streaming service over the holidays.

Set eight years after the events of “Once Upon a Time “in Hollywood,” the film follows former stuntman Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt). Having stepped away from stunt work, Cliff now earns a living as a bartender, using his unconventional skills to handle problems for the entertainment industry’s biggest names. When talent agent Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki) approaches him on behalf of television star Charlie Peters (Scott Caan), Cliff becomes involved in a complicated situation involving Charlie’s wife Toni (Carla Gugino) and two mysterious gangster brothers causing trouble across the city.

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" hits theaters on Nov. 25

For something with a much bloodier take on Christmas, “Violent Night 2” should be on your radar next month. David Harbour returns as the hard-hitting Santa Claus, with Kristen Bell joining the cast for a new round of festive action. The sequel comes from the production company behind “Nobody 2” and “The Fall Guy,” so there’s good reason to expect plenty of inventive stuntwork and over-the-top fight scenes. Its reported influences include classic Spaghetti Westerns and traditional holiday movies, which sounds like an entertaining combination.

Santa Claus (David Harbour) returns for another Christmas showdown when a ruthless gangster (Jared Harris) and his armed henchmen take over the Silver Bell Mall. Stranded away from the North Pole and stripped of his magical powers, Santa must find another way to protect the mall’s merchants and the surrounding community. With time running out and his usual abilities no longer available, he’ll need to rely on his fighting skills to take down the criminals. Fortunately, he won’t be tackling the job alone, as Mrs. Claus (Kristen Bell) arrives to help him fight back.

"Violent Night 2" hits theaters on Dec. 4

“Avengers: Doomsday” is undoubtedly one of the biggest and most anticipated movies of the year, and I’m very curious to see what Marvel has planned. The Russo brothers return to the MCU for the first time since “Endgame,” reuniting with longtime collaborator Stephen McFeely to direct this next chapter and its follow-up, “Secret Wars.” As the 39th film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, there’s a lot riding on this one, particularly with Doctor Doom stepping into the spotlight as a major threat. I’m incredibly excited to see how it all unfolds, but also a little nervous about just how brutal Doom could be.

The Avengers face their biggest challenge yet when a powerful new enemy threatens multiple universes. Led by Victor von Doom (Robert Downey Jr.), the looming crisis brings together heroes from across the Marvel universe, including the Avengers, Fantastic Four, X-Men and Wakandans. As their worlds are set on a collision course, the unlikely allies must confront a threat capable of changing the fate of the multiverse. With familiar faces including Thor (Chris Hemsworth), Steve Rogers (Chris Evans), Shuri (Letitia Wright) and Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal), the heroes must find a way to stop Doom before it’s too late.

"Avengers: Doomsday" hits theaters Dec. 18

Another huge film releasing next month and competing on the same day with “Doomsday” is “Dune 3.” Denis Villeneuve returns to direct what is expected to be the final chapter of his Arrakis saga, adapting Frank Herbert’s 1969 novel “Dune Messiah.” Rather than simply serving as a traditional trilogy finale, Villeneuve has described the film as more of an epilogue to Paul Atreides’ story, bringing his journey to a close while taking the franchise in a new direction. With the previous two movies proving such huge cinematic events, this is easily one of the biggest releases over the holiday season.

“Dune 3” continues the story of Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet) following his rise to power on Arrakis. Set several years after the events of part 2, the film follows Paul as he rules as Emperor, while facing growing opposition to his reign and the consequences of the religious movement that has spread across the universe in his name. As rival factions secretly plot to overthrow him, Paul must contend with dangerous new enemies and a mysterious conspiracy involving the Bene Tleilax. Meanwhile, Chani (Zendaya) finds herself caught up in events that could change the future of House Atreides.

“Jumanji: Open World” brings the modern rebooted franchise to a close, reuniting audiences with its familiar mix of action, comedy and adventure. The latest instalment looks set to shake up the formula by bringing the game’s dangers into the real world, rather than transporting its characters into a virtual jungle. That means wild animals, chaotic stampedes and other game hazards spilling into everyday suburban and urban settings. It’s an interesting twist on the series’ familiar setup, and a promising way to wrap up this latest chapter of the “Jumanji” franchise.

The group are reunited for another adventure when the Jumanji video game unexpectedly escapes its console and spills into the real world. As wild animals and dangerous creatures wreak havoc, the game’s familiar avatars, Dr. Smolder Bravestone (Dwayne Johnson), Ruby Roundhouse (Karen Gillan), Mouse Finbar (Kevin Hart) and Professor Shelly Oberon (Jack Black), find themselves roaming the streets in demo mode. With the game threatening to turn everyday life upside down, the group must return to Jumanji and find a way to stop the chaos.

"Jumanji: Open World" hits theaters on Dec. 25

One of my most anticipated films of 2026 in general is “Werwulf,” the period gothic folk-horror feature directed by Robert Eggers. Following “Nosferatu,” the director is taking on another creature-focused story, this time set in a period setting with a folk-horror twist. It also reunites several familiar faces from his previous film, including Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Lily-Rose Depp, Willem Dafoe and Ralph Ineson. Eggers is co-writing with Sjón, marking their second collaboration after “The Northman,” and has described the screenplay as the darkest he's written so far.

Set in 13th-century England, “Werwulf” follows a mute medieval farmer (Aaron Taylor-Johnson) who lives quietly with his family while hiding a terrifying secret: he transforms into a murderous werewolf whenever the full moon rises. When a hunting party arrives under the king’s orders to eliminate the wolves roaming the countryside, the farmer is forced to join them, putting his secret at risk. As the hunters search for the creature responsible for a series of attacks, he struggles to conceal his identity while protecting his wife and children from the growing danger.

Alix is a Senior Streaming Writer at Tom’s Guide, which basically means watching the best movies and TV shows and then writing about them. It’s a dream job for someone who’s been obsessed with storytelling since she first figured out how to work a remote.

Before joining Tom’s Guide, Alix honed her skills as a staff writer with outlets like Screen Rant and Bough Digital, where she discovered her love for the entertainment industry.

She heads to the cinema every week as a tradition, no matter what’s showing. For her, movies aren’t just entertainment — they’re a ritual, a comfort, and a constant source of inspiration. When she’s not at her desk or at the cinema, you’ll probably find her deep into a horror video game on her PC.

#3339. Apple announces Swift Student Challenge 2027 with new twist

Apple has announced details for 2027’s Swift Student Challenge, and there’s a new twist this year: students can submit an app for any Apple platform.

Apple is proud to support the next generation of developers, creators, and entrepreneurs with the Swift Student Challenge. The Challenge gives students from around the world the opportunity to showcase their creativity and app development skills.

Submissions are open February 8–28, 2027. And new this year, students can submit an app for any Apple platform. Sign up now to get notifications about student activities.

February 8-28 is still a few months away, but Apple wants to give participants plenty of time to plan ahead and start working on their entry sooner rather than later.

And in an exciting change, students can build an app for any platform this year, including tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, and more.

This opens fresh opportunities for creativity, especially on Apple’s less saturated app platforms.

Apple will once again recognize winners across two tiers: “winners” and “distinguished winners.” The latter will be invited to join Apple in Cupertino “for an incredible experience.” All winners will receive a one-year Apple Developer program membership and a special gift.

Will you participate in the Swift Student Challenge this coming year? Let us know in the comments.

#3338. 'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

Grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time. It's been 13 years since Rockstar dropped GTA 5, and after years of rumors, leaks, and official announcements, the sixth mainstream installment in the series is nearly here. In fact, anyone who pre-ordered the game digitally can now pre-load it onto their console, if you want to ensure you're ready to play the second the game comes out.

Now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox. (The PC version of the game isn't expected until at least early 2027.) But, as it turns out, there's one specific console that can run GTA 6 better than the rest.

Rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game. But, interestingly, it spurred a discussion about the performance of the game itself, as well as which consoles are best to run it.

No matter which console you play GTA 6 on, Rockstar says that the game will only target 30 fps (frames per second). That's decided slow for a mainstream game in 2026. GTA 5 also shipped at 30 fps in 2013, but newer consoles can run it at higher frame rates. In fact, most games that launch on the latest generation of consoles can run at 60 fps, if not higher. While it's certainly not a dealbreaker, it is interesting that Rockstar's latest game can't run at a faster frame rate even on the PS5 Pro or the Xbox Series X.

To that point, Rockstar called out the PS5 Pro specifically in its post, announcing, "The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro."

PSSR is Sony's AI upscaler, similar to options like DLSS from Nvidia, which uses AI to add extra graphical information to games in real time. That allows developers like Rockstar to run the game at a lower resolution to save on processing power, but still boost the visuals to reach a higher perceived resolution. As such, it's not as ideal as running the game at a higher resolution natively, but it can help improve the visuals without pushing the hardware beyond its limits. Meanwhile, ray-tracing offers realistic lighting effects and can also be graphically intense.

While PlayStation and Xbox players alike will be stuck at 30 fps, it seems only PS5 Pro gamers will be able to play the game with ray-tracing effects and AI upscaling. It's surprising that Xbox Series X players don't have similar benefits, as the hardware is more powerful than Xbox Series S. Rockstar didn't specify why only the PS5 Pro gets these upgrades.

In the post, Rockstar also announced that the PS5 version of GTA 6 takes advantage of other PlayStation-exclusive perks, like high-fidelity haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, spatial audio rendering using the PlayStation's Tempest 3D audio, as well as improved load times—though Rockstar didn't specify what those load times would be. These perks apply to all PS5 consoles, not just PS5 Pros. Rockstar goes so far as to say that GTA 6 plays best on PlayStation 5 consoles.

That's not to say that Microsoft's consoles are totally left out of the perks. Rockstar says that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on both Xbox Series X and S, as well as Xbox One. In addition, both PlayStation and Xbox gamers can play GTA 6 using Remote Play, so no one has to physically play on their console if they want to game on the go.

Again, there's no reason to go out and buy a specific console for GTA 6, so long as you have something that can run the game. After all, PS5 Pros are difficult to find, especially without wildly overpaying. But it's interesting that Rockstar has managed to give Sony's consoles the extra perks here, particularly since the company hasn't explained why that is.

#3337. The 35+ Best Gifts for Moms, According to My Mother’s Mini Me (Yours Truly)

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

They say mother knows best, and when it comes to gift-giving, mine really does. My mom has always had a flair for whimsy. She’s the kind of woman who would lay an entire tarp across our backyard on the last day of school and stage a food fight, or build a Christmas countdown calendar from scratch, then fill every little compartment with surprises.

She’s also the reason I learned that the best gifts aren’t necessarily the ones people ask for, but the ones they didn’t even know they needed. Turns out, that lesson would come in handy when I made gift-giving my career.

My mom is truly the best human on the planet. Don’t worry, I’m sure yours is, too. Which is why I want to help you find a present she’ll love when the holidays roll around.

So, where do you start shopping? I’d steer clear of the obvious. Sure, a robe is nice. A scarf will keep her warm. Another water bottle? She probably has six. You can do better! This is the woman who taught you how to make the most out of life, after all. She deserves something as one-of-a-kind as your relationship. Maybe that’s a cuckoo clock you can build together or a custom garden gnome with her face on it. Whatever fills her cup, there’s something here that’ll make her smile.

I also kept budgets, interests, and personalities in mind, because no two moms — or gift-givers — are alike. Hanukkah, Christmas, and some of the biggest shopping holidays of the year are fast approaching (and didn’t your mom teach you that early is always better than on time?). So consider this your friendly nudge to get shopping. For Hanukkah, aim to have your gifts sorted by around Nov. 20, roughly two weeks before the holiday. For Christmas, I’d try to wrap things up by Dec. 12.

Shop my 35+ best gifts for your mom below, and give her something she’ll actually want to show off to her friends. You know, something other than another photo of you.

Cozy Earth pajamas have been one of the most popular products in all of our holiday gift guides, and for good reason. Between their near-unreasonable level of softness and my own personal devotion to them, they had to make this list too. They run true to size, but if you’re debating sizing up, I say go for it. The worst thing that can happen is she ends up even more comfortable.

Gorjana makes stunning birthstone bracelets that you can customize with stones representing her kids, grandkids, or whoever else has earned a spot. Or, you can leave everyone else off and just include yourself… A subtle way to remind her who her favorite child is.

If your mom spends as much time in the garden as she does with your dad — potentially more, no judgment — get her a custom garden gnome with her face on it. All you have to do is provide a photo, and Printerval handles the rest.

Have you hugged your mom recently? If not, I’m going to need you to get on that. But even the most devoted children can’t be there all the time, and sometimes she might need a little extra comfort when you’re not around. This Bearaby weighted blanket is a pretty good stand-in. Just don’t let it replace an actual phone call.

This might be one of the sweetest gifts you can buy your mom this holiday season because chances are she owned a version of this Lenox Spice Village when she was little, or her mom did. Either way, it’s the kind of nostalgic gift that can transport her back to simpler times while also giving her kitchen a very cute upgrade. My mother-in-law had the original, so I got her this modern version for Christmas this year (and Cara, if you see this, pretend you didn’t).

If you thought Tommy Bahama only made resort wear for vacations in the Bahamas, allow me to introduce you to the brand’s winter staples. This fleece jacket is insanely comfortable, and I own multiple Tommy Bahama sweaters that have convinced me the quality is the real deal. Take my word for it; I shop for a living.

My mom reads about three books a week, no exaggeration, so making sure she never loses her place is practically a public service. I got her this page-saving cottage lamp, which doubles as a cute little bedside accessory. It adds a bit of whimsy to her literary world and means she can stop folding the corners of her books. (Please tell her not to do that.)

And since she’s so obsessed with reading, I also got her this literature mug from Uncommon Goods, which happens to be one of my favorite places to find genuinely unique gifts. She just has to scan it with her phone (and if she doesn’t have an upgraded smartphone yet, maybe that’s your next gift) to hear from some of the world’s greatest literary minds whenever she wants.

Treat your mom to tea for two (with you, obviously) by buying her this stunning Spode china set. It’s currently on sale at Macy’s, and as someone who was recently gifted her own set of nice china, I can tell you that opening a box like this might just take her breath away. Which, really, is how you win Christmas. Not that it’s a competition…

For that beautiful china you just got her, help her preserve it with this stunning display cabinet from Ashley Furniture. It fits perfectly into just about any corner of her home and gives her a place to show off all of her favorite mementos. Maybe your eighth-grade art project won’t make the cut, but her mother’s wedding spoon might.

So, yes, this might be one of the more basic Christmas gifts on the list, but you seriously can’t go wrong with getting your mom a pair of house shoes. And if you’re going to do it, make them UGGs. They’re a chic way to give her slippers that feel a little more thoughtful than the random pair you panic-bought from a massive online retailer two days before Christmas.

This is a more practical gift for your mom, but it’s also one she probably didn’t know existed or that she needed. Memory Air works by releasing scented puffs while she sleeps and claims to do everything from helping her get more ZZZs at night to supporting memory, according to the brand. Plus, it’s backed by Doctors, so your mom doesn’t have to worry that this is another random thing you were served in a suspicious Instagram ad. I regret the minute I ever told my mom about those.

For the moms who love birdwatching, this high-tech feeder lets her see who’s making a pit stop through a connected app. It can even help identify the species, which is a whole lot easier than trying to describe a bird to an AI website and hoping for the right answer.

My mom has been making us pajama pants for Christmas for as long as I can remember, so I recently decided to upgrade her sewing machine and make her job a little easier. She hasn’t stopped telling me how much she loves this model. It’s great for easy projects, more challenging ones, and even the things she didn’t know were possible. Her mom used a Singer, my mom uses a Singer, and I use a Singer, too. Three generations in, I think we can call that a family endorsement.

My mom and I went to Austria together in September and walked into a cuckoo clock shop. We both knew immediately that we had to buy one. If your mom shares the same wandering spirit as the two of us, get her one she can build herself — or, even better, one you can help her put together. Consider it an excuse to spend a little more time together.

If your mom is the kind of woman who would happily spend the rest of her life in comfortable clothes, you’re doing her a disservice by not getting her this Aviator Nation sweatshirt and matching sweatpants. It delivers everything she loves about her favorite sweatshirt, just in a version she can actually leave the house in. The one with your childhood fingerprints all over it is cute, but maybe it’s time to move that one into the memory box.

Tinggly is one of my personal gifting hacks because it gives your mom more than another thing to unwrap under the tree; it gives her an experience. And, realistically, the thing she probably wants most is to spend time with you. A weekend getaway is a pretty great way to make that happen. This package lets her choose from multiple destinations, so you can give her the R&R she deserves without pretending you know exactly where she wants to go.

If I had to guess, your mom has been carrying the same tired shoulder bag for approximately a decade. Give her a much-deserved upgrade with this Rebecca Minkoff and Grace Ann Nader hobo bag. Bonus points if she’s a Real Housewives fan, since Rebecca Minkoff is a RHONY alum.

My mom is always asking me about my skincare routine, and instead of giving her my full Get Ready With Me speech every time she brings it up, I finally just sent her the link to this Water Whip moisturizer. It’s a no-frills but extremely functional way to keep your skin looking close to perfect, and now she uses it every morning and, apparently, has made it her personal mission to tell all of her friends about it too.

Even dog moms are mothers, so if you’re shopping for the woman in your life who treats her pet like her actual baby (as she should), this Lola dog bed (yes, that Lola) will help her spoil her little furry bundle of joy accordingly. Since getting one for my dog, he hasn’t left it for more than 20 minutes at a time. Plus, I appreciate how good it actually looks in my home, which is something I can’t say about every dog bed.

Brilliant Earth has some of our favorite gift ideas for Mom, but this special necklace is as tasteful as it gets. It’s dainty, affordable, and best of all, it comes from you. Pearls supposedly symbolize motherhood and everlasting love, so what better way to put that sentiment into something tangible than with this pendant?

I recently got my mom this bedding bundle, and one morning I woke up to a text that read: “OMG, OMG, OMG, this is the best set of sheets ever!!!! I didn’t want to get out of bed!! Do I have to go to work?? LOL.” True story. So, if you want to wake up to a similarly enthusiastic review from your own mother, this is a pretty safe bet.

Myles Price makes sweatshirts for every kind of mom, especially the hot mamas who want to be comfortable but still look like they have their lives together. She’ll be the envy of every other parent at school pickup, and almost definitely the most comfortable one there.

I feel a little guilty about this one. I’ve known about Lola Blankets for a while now, own multiple, and am about as obsessed with them as the rest of the internet. Then my mom called me the other day to say she saw one on TV and was dying to get one…. Something I probably should have gotten her months ago. Well, I immediately ordered it, and now it’s on its way. Learn from my mistakes and do the same for your mother before it’s too late and they sell out of her Christmas list.

My mom has been wearing this scent for decades, and she always told me that you can never go wrong with Chanel. You know what? She was right (as she is about a lot of things). This was also reportedly one of Marilyn Monroe’s favorite scents, and while some gentlemen might prefer blondes, your mom will probably prefer this perfume.

Getting your mom another picture of yourself is so last year. What she really wants under the tree is a portrait of her dog as a member of the royal court. I was gifted one of these a few years ago and have been slowly getting them for all of my family members ever since. My mom hangs hers in what she calls her parlor, also known as the billiards room. Whatever you call the room, this deserves a spot in it.

For the moms who are fans of The Mary Tyler Moore Show, you can now get her some of the most iconic looks she saw on screen, thanks to this collaboration with Frances Valentine. How’s that for actually paying attention to her hobbies and getting her something she probably wouldn’t think to buy herself?

If you have a wife who recently became a mom, get her these Hot Mom socks so she can remember exactly who the hell she is, even in the thick of postpartum life. Did I send this link to my brother so he could get them for his wife, who just had a baby? Yes. Do I know she’ll appreciate the reminder? More than you think. Take it from a woman.

My mom and I ran our first-ever 5K in Brooks sneakers, and while we might not be adding marathons to our regularly scheduled mother-daughter activities anytime soon, one thing we’ll continue doing together is wearing Brooks. They’re the only sneakers my mom will buy, and considering she works retail and spends eight hours a day on her feet, I trust her judgment.

Your mom is already the head of your family’s team, but if she has another team she roots for — or a specific player she loves, like Josh Allen (all moms love him, it’s a fact) — help her show her support with a cute sweatshirt from ’47 and Stoney Clover Lane. They run slightly bigger than your average crewneck, so size down if she prefers a more fitted look.

Moms everywhere are obsessed with mahjong. That might be a generalization, but I know mine is, as are all of my aunts and cousins who are moms. Help her get in on the game-night action with a set of her very own. She’ll be the most popular person at the next family gathering.

I always say you should buy your mom a pair of recovery slides from Nike because they help her take a load off, quite literally. But then I found this upgraded version from Nike x Hyperice that actually heats up and massages her feet. Yeah, that’s an automatic win.

If your mom is obsessed with all things Disney, pay tribute to one of her favorite pastimes with this Lilly Pulitzer and Disney dress. It’s a little less Mickey Mouse and a little more subtly infused magic, thanks to a classic Lilly Pulitzer silhouette she can wear outside the parks, too.

My mom is always cold. She probably doesn’t realize that she spent 20 years of her life sitting through my brothers’ ice hockey games, but I’m pretty sure that’s where it started. So I got her this Carhartt jacket, which manages to keep her at just the right temperature even during a brutal New Hampshire winter. If anyone knows how to dress for a chilly day, it’s a hockey mom.

At some point in time, your mom will become obsessed with her family tree (if it hasn’t happened already). The day my mom told me we were distantly related to a European king was the greatest day of her life, which only mildly concerned me. Help her dig into her past with an Ancestry DNA kit. You never know who your mom might discover she’s related to, or which royal family she might try to claim as her own.

For the moms whose love language is a Sunday supper (which was definitely my nanny’s), get her these world-class pans from Eater and Heritage Steel. She can whip up anything, from meatballs to her own top-secret gravy recipe, and you’ll benefit from the results. Or, better yet, make her a meal with them. She deserves it, after all.

This gift is for both the moms who love to garden and those who want to but might not exactly have a green thumb. I’ll tell you this: When I first bought one for myself, I was skeptical. But it supplied my husband and me with six months of the freshest vegetables I’ve ever tasted, after which I immediately ordered more seedling pods. When my parents found out about it, they ordered one, too, and my mom says she’d never go back to traditional gardening. That’s a pretty strong endorsement.

#3336. Apple has new Mac app coming to make running local AI models easy

Leaker Aaron Perris has discovered evidence of a new Mac app in the works at Apple called Harbor, which makes it easy to run local AI models across one or more Macs.

The Mac has been getting a lot more popular this year, both because of budget-friendly options like MacBook Neo but also as a tool for running AI models locally on Mac Studio, Mac mini, and more.

It seems Apple plans to lean harder into the latter use case, as leaker Aaron Perris has discovered a new Mac app called Harbor that’s been designed to turn your Mac into a private AI inference server.

Here’s Perris’s post on X with the details:

Apple is working on a new app called HarborHarbor turns your Mac into a private AI inference server. Run open-weight models locally on Apple silicon—your data never leaves your hardware, and nothing reaches the cloud. Connect multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool… pic.twitter.com/UYJBQeX4Nf

As the post notes, here’s what the app does:

Harbor turns your Mac into a private AI inference server. Run open-weight models locally on Apple silicon—your data never leaves your hardware, and nothing reaches the cloud. Connect multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory, enabling large models and higher concurrency that a single computer can handle alone.

Harbor is currently in a private preview under Apple’s Claris brand, but it seems likely that we’ll see it launch to the public in the weeks and months ahead.

Are you interested in using Harbor on your Mac? Let us know in the comments.

#3334. Lifehacker's Pick for the Best TV to Gift in 2026 Isn't Actually a TV

Welcome to Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, a collaborative multimedia project in which Lifehacker, CNET, ZDNET, and Mashable harness the power of our product testing laboratory and our editors' expertise to offer the best gift-buying recommendations possible. In this episode, we're talking televisions.

I recently did a deep dive into TV development history, checked out what was on shelves for 2026, and I concluded that the best gift TV you can give this year is, actually, a pair of sunglasses. The XBX by XReal video display glasses are basically a TV you can shove in your pocket. Check them out:

I looked past traditional sets for a couple of reasons. First, because as much as we all love a great show or movie, who actually buys someone a TV set as a gift? More importantly, there's the nature of television itself. Since it was invented in the late 1920s, television quality has been measured by how big the screen is and how clear and bright the picture is, but in 2026, a nothing-special 4K television delivers an image that is pixel-invisible to a typical viewer, and most of us don't have living rooms big enough to need a display bigger than 65 inches. I think the innovation in the space is going to come from the form factor and the use case, and what better form factor is there than a pair of sunglasses?

These glasses deliver the equivalent of a 142" TV viewed from across the room. It's hard to compare resolution to traditional TVs—technically, the display is 1080p in each eye, but because the TV is just millimeters from your eye, it looks much clearer than that. The peak brightness is 1,600 nits, bright enough for most rooms, and there's a totally opaque shield if you need it. The refresh rate is a crisp 120Hz. They support HDR10 and real-time SDR-to-HDR upscaling, offer billions of colors, and it's all in a package that weighs only 62 grams.

Then there are the use cases. It can act as a separate monitor for your computer; you can watch a different show than your roommate without bothering them; but most of all, these are great for flights. There is no situation in life that calls for a big screen TV more than a cross-country airplane flight. Slip these on with a pair of headphones, and you can fly to Boise in your own private, virtual theater.

They plug right into any device that supports USB-C video, there's no battery to remember to charge, and they cost less than $300. In other words: They're the perfect TV gift for the holidays, even if they aren't technically a TV.

#3333. iOS 27.2 adds new features in six iPhone apps, details here

iOS 27.2 recently launched with new features for iPhone users, including improvements across six Apple apps. Here’s what’s new.

One of my favorite additions to Messages this year, Suggested Actions, debuts in iOS 27.2.

Suggested Actions appear underneath messages in a conversation when relevant. They can suggest creating a calendar event or reminder, adding to a note, and more based on the context of the message.

The feature was originally part of the iOS 27 beta this summer, but didn’t make the public build. Now it’s back in iOS 27.2, new and improved. There’s also an option to fine-tune which types of suggestions you’ll see.

Read more: iOS 27.2 adds new Messages feature that’s already a favorite

Every major streaming service has its own profiles feature, letting users on the same account keep their viewing history and recommendations separate. Apple TV has long offered such a feature in tvOS, but now with iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 it’s coming to iPhone and iPad too.

When you launch the TV app in iOS 27.2, you’ll be greeted by a new profile selection screen. You can easily disable it if you don’t want to see if again. But if you ever share your iPhone with kids, the new profiles feature should come in handy.

Read more: iOS 27.2 gives Apple TV a new profiles feature on iPhone

Dual Capture is one of FaceTime’s best new features in years. Added in iOS 27, on compatible iPhones it lets you keep your front and rear cameras both active at the same time while on a FaceTime call.

iOS 27.2 brings a key upgrade to Dual Capture: it’s now available for Group FaceTime calls.

To use the feature, just hit the flip camera button like usual, and by default on iPhone 17 and newer you’ll stream both camera feeds simultaneously.

Read more: iOS 27.2 makes FaceTime’s best new feature even better

Timed with its new Home products push, Apple adds a pair of new Home app features in iOS 27.2 for compatible smart locks.

‘Lock After Closing’ is a new automation setting that lets you choose how long after a door is closed that it should lock automatically. Previously you could only set a duration based on the time since a door was unlocked, not closed.

‘Door Left Open’ tackles a related, but distinct problem: a door being left open too long. With compatible locks, you can configure the Home app to automatically notify you if a door has been left open for a certain period of time.

Read more: iOS 27.2 has three new changes just added this week

Apple Podcasts keeps getting better, with AI-powered automatic chapters and transcripts some of my favorite features. And in iOS 27.2, Apple has a welcome change to the Up Next queue on the Home tab.

Up Next is now split into two separate queues: New Episodes and Continue Playing.

Without the redesigned Health app, none of the new features appeal to me all that much. But performance improvements, bug fixes, and security fixes are always welcomed. What most of really wants is faster and more reliable Siri AI, along with support for a wider range of personal data, such as PDF documents on the iCloud Drive.

New Episodes contains only the latest episodes from shows you follow, while Continue Playing is a hub for all the episodes you’ve previously started but haven’t yet finished.

Apple’s Games app introduces some small updates in iOS 27.2 as well.

The Home tab now shows you recently downloaded games that you haven’t yet played. Previously, you would only see games with some play activity. And Apple says achievement progress and leaderboard scores have been updated in the Home tab to be easier to track. Finally, the Friends tab “provides context on friend suggestions and shows recent games played on friends’ player pages” per Apple.

Which new iOS 27.2 features are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments.

“I’ve never had any time off,” Wood tells Rolling Stone by phone hours before taking the stage at Teatro Caupolicán in Santiago, Chile, for the final show of his South American tour. ”Now that the Stones have got a little sabbatical, I’m making the most of it and keeping my chops together, using my fingers, and getting the blood running. It’s such a buzz, physically and mentally.”

He’s especially excited to play the Beacon. “It’s a special place,” Wood says. “I saw Al Green there, and we played there with Stones [in 2006]. I want to notch it up on my solo podium.”

Wood has been backed by a group of musicians that he’s dubbed the Ammo Band, which includes bassist Willie Weeks, drummer Andy Newmark, keyboardist Andy Wallace, guitarist Johnny Lee Schell, and Rolling Stones background vocalist Chanel Haynes. Weeks and Newmark both worked with Wood on his 1974 solo debut I’ve Got My Own Album to Do. “We’re all still alive,” Wood says, “and all still grooving better than ever.”

Wood first met Haynes in 2022 when Stones background singer Sasha Allen had to miss a show in Milan, and Haynes flew in at the last second to join them for “Gimme Shelter.” She did such a stellar job that the Stones used her on their 2024 Hackney Diamonds tour for both “Gimme Shelter” and “Sweet Sounds of Heaven.” And on Wood’s tour, she has even more moments at the center of the stage. “She’s amazing,” says Wood. “She sings a bunch of songs, and joins me on the harmonies.”

#3331. Atomically Thin Materials Significantly Shrink Qubits

MIT researchers use 2D materials for capacitors in quantum circuits in an effort to scale processors

Superconducting quantum processor and its microwave packaging.

Quantum computing is a devilishly complex technology, with many technical hurdles impacting its development. Of these challenges two critical issues stand out: miniaturization and qubit quality.

IBM has adopted the superconducting qubit road map of reaching a 1,121-qubit processor by 2023, leading to the expectation that 1,000 qubits with today’s qubit form factor is feasible. However, current approaches will require very large chips (50 millimeters on a side, or larger) at the scale of small wafers, or the use of chiplets on multichip modules. While this approach will work, the aim is to attain a better path toward scalability.

Now researchers at MIT have been able to both reduce the size of the qubits and done so in a way that reduces the interference that occurs between neighboring qubits. The MIT researchers have increased the number of superconducting qubits that can be added onto a device by a factor of 100.

“We are addressing both qubit miniaturization and quality,” said William Oliver, the director for the Center for Quantum Engineering at MIT. “Unlike conventional transistor scaling, where only the number really matters, for qubits, large numbers are not sufficient, they must also be high-performance. Sacrificing performance for qubit number is not a useful trade in quantum computing. They must go hand in hand.”

The key to this big increase in qubit density and reduction of interference comes down to the use of two-dimensional materials, in particular the 2D insulator hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). The MIT researchers demonstrated that a few atomic monolayers of hBN can be stacked to form the insulator in the capacitors of a superconducting qubit.

Just like other capacitors, the capacitors in these superconducting circuits take the form of a sandwich in which an insulator material is sandwiched between two metal plates. The big difference for these capacitors is that the superconducting circuits can operate only at extremely low temperatures—less than 0.02 degrees above absolute zero (-273.15 °C).

Superconducting qubits are measured at temperatures as low as 20 millikelvin in a dilution refrigerator.Nathan Fiske/MIT

In that environment, insulating materials that are available for the job, such as PE-CVD silicon oxide or silicon nitride, have quite a few defects that are too lossy for quantum computing applications. To get around these material shortcomings, most superconducting circuits use what are called coplanar capacitors. In these capacitors, the plates are positioned laterally to one another, rather than on top of one another.

As a result, the intrinsic silicon substrate below the plates and to a smaller degree the vacuum above the plates serve as the capacitor dielectric. Intrinsic silicon is chemically pure and therefore has few defects, and the large size dilutes the electric field at the plate interfaces, all of which leads to a low-loss capacitor. The lateral size of each plate in this open-face design ends up being quite large (typically 100 by 100 micrometers) in order to achieve the required capacitance.

In an effort to move away from the large lateral configuration, the MIT researchers embarked on a search for an insulator that has very few defects and is compatible with superconducting capacitor plates.

“We chose to study hBN because it is the most widely used insulator in 2D material research due to its cleanliness and chemical inertness,” said colead author Joel Wang, a research scientist in the Engineering Quantum Systems group of the MIT Research Laboratory for Electronics.

On either side of the hBN, the MIT researchers used the 2D superconducting material, niobium diselenide. One of the trickiest aspects of fabricating the capacitors was working with the niobium diselenide, which oxidizes in seconds when exposed to air, according to Wang. This necessitates that the assembly of the capacitor occur in a glove box filled with argon gas.

While this would seemingly complicate the scaling up of the production of these capacitors, Wang doesn’t regard this as a limiting factor.

“What determines the quality factor of the capacitor are the two interfaces between the two materials,” said Wang. “Once the sandwich is made, the two interfaces are “sealed” and we don’t see any noticeable degradation over time when exposed to the atmosphere.”

This lack of degradation is because around 90 percent of the electric field is contained within the sandwich structure, so the oxidation of the outer surface of the niobium diselenide does not play a significant role anymore. This ultimately makes the capacitor footprint much smaller, and it accounts for the reduction in cross talk between the neighboring qubits.

“The main challenge for scaling up the fabrication will be the wafer-scale growth of hBN and 2D superconductors like [niobium diselenide], and how one can do wafer-scale stacking of these films,” added Wang.

Wang believes that this research has shown 2D hBN to be a good insulator candidate for superconducting qubits. He says that the groundwork the MIT team has done will serve as a road map for using other hybrid 2D materials to build superconducting circuits.

Dexter Johnson is a contributing editor at IEEE Spectrum, with a focus on nanotechnology.

#3330. What to Expect From Best Buy's 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday Sales

For all intents and purposes, Black Friday sales are already here. There are plenty of deals out already, even though we're weeks away from the actual event. One of the reasons for that is the competition retailers have with each other to be the first to get your money. One of the retailers that is making the biggest early splash is Best Buy, confirming their entire plan for the rest of the year. Here's what you need to know.

Best Buy has announced the following events:

DoorBoosters: A Halloween sale from Oct. 30 to Nov. 1.

Early Black Friday Deals and Doorbusters: The official start of early Black Friday deals on Nov. 6. New deals will drop every Friday.

Black Friday Doorbusters and Deals: Best Buy says this will be its main sale, starting on Thursday, Nov. 19 and running until Nov. 28 with deals on "computing, gaming, home theater, wearables, and more."

Cyber Sunday and Monday: Best Buy is extending Cyber Monday to five days and says you can find deals going up to 50% off select tech.

Last-minute savings: The Christmas sale will run from Dec. 18 until Dec. 24.

You don't need to be any kind of member to shop Best Buy's Black Friday in July sale; however, it is free to sign up for a My Best Buy membership, which will get you free shipping. If you join one of their paid subscriptions (My Best Buy Plus for $49.99 per year or My Best Buy Total for $179.99 per year), you'll get faster free shipping, exclusive prices and deals, an extended 60-day return window on most products, and access to select sales, like the Member Deals Days sale that is going on right now. Paid members will also earn extra rewards from both the current sale and the upcoming Black Friday in July sale.

You can find deals on TVs, laptops, headphones, video games, electric bikes, and more. There will be new deals every week in stores, on its website, and in the Best Buy mobile app. They'll offer price matching, meaning if the price drops further during the sale (Dec. 24), they will match it and offer a refund.

Best Buy price matches its own products, so if a product drops in price later, you'd get those savings too, but it does not cover any deals coming from a competitor's Black Friday sale. There are some other important exceptions you can read in more detail here.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

The other major retailers doing Black Friday sales are Amazon, Target, and Walmart. Currently, Amazon has many early deals, seeing their lowest prices yet. Target has some week-long deals and a Deal of the Day. Walmart will have three Black Friday and Cyber Monday shopping events. Nowadays, large retailers and small businesses compete for Cyber Monday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026.

Advocacy groups want AI stopped and safeguards put in place

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The backlash against AI is getting harder for Silicon Valley to ignore. Just days after five people were arrested protesting Anthropic's planned IPO, a coalition of advocacy groups has filed a lawsuit seeking to stop some of the world's biggest AI companies from developing and releasing new models.

The lawsuit, filed Thursday in San Francisco Superior Court, targets OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceXSI. The groups behind it argue that the companies are advancing technology that could cause catastrophic harm without adequate safeguards.

For consumers who use ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini every day, the case raises a question about the future of AI. Could the companies responsible for today's most popular chatbots eventually be forced to slow down?

The lawsuit comes from four nonprofit organizations: the Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, Heat Initiative and the Alliance for Secure AI.

According to The Associated Press, the complaint alleges that the companies have violated California's unfair competition law by endangering public health and interfering with people's use of property, including computer systems.

The groups point to reported incidents involving AI-assisted cyberattacks and warn that increasingly autonomous systems could eventually operate beyond human control.

They want a judge to prevent the five companies from developing or deploying new AI models.

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

This represents an effort to use the courts to impose limits on an industry that has expanded rapidly over the past several years with very few safeguards.

The lawsuit follows another development involving Anthropic, the company behind Claude.

On Monday, November 9, protesters gathered outside Anthropic's Manhattan offices to oppose its planned initial public offering, which could value the company at approximately $1.4 trillion.

According to Democracy Now!, five protesters were arrested after blocking an employee security entrance.

The demonstration involved activists from Climate Defenders, New York Communities for Change and Planet Over Profit. Their concerns focused on the financial risks surrounding the AI industry, including the possibility that soaring valuations could contribute to a wider economic downturn.

According to a report shared with Tom's Guide, activist Jonathan Westin told Democracy Now! that he feared Anthropic and the wider AI industry could crash the global economy.

Unlike Thursday's lawsuit, which focuses on technological safety, the demonstration targeted the financial consequences of the AI boom.

These risks have been mentioned before. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has previously acknowledged the possibility of AI development going badly and called for the industry to slow the pace of progress so safety measures can catch up.

Yet Anthropic continues developing increasingly advanced AI systems while preparing for a potentially historic public offering.

That tension is becoming harder to ignore as the industry moves toward AI agents capable of performing complex tasks, interacting with computer systems and operating with less human supervision.

For now, nothing changes about how consumers can use these chatbots. The lawsuit is an attempt to prevent future AI development, not an order requiring companies to shut down existing products or suspend subscriptions.

But if the plaintiffs ultimately succeed in obtaining a broad court order, the consequences could extend well beyond Silicon Valley. New model launches, advanced AI features and the pace of competition between companies could all be affected.

#3327. How AI Will Change Chip Design

Artificial intelligence’s promise and potential for the semiconductor industry

Rina Diane Caballar is a contributing editor covering tech and its intersections with science, society, and the environment.

An array of semiconductor wafers are ready to be made into chips.

The end of Moore’s Law is looming. Engineers and designers can do only so much to miniaturize transistors and pack as many of them as possible into chips. So they’re turning to other approaches to chip design, incorporating technologies like AI into the process.

Samsung, for instance, is adding AI to its memory chips to enable processing in memory, thereby saving energy and speeding up machine learning. Speaking of speed, Google’s TPU V4 AI chip has doubled its processing power compared with that of its previous version.

But AI holds still more promise and potential for the semiconductor industry. To better understand how AI is set to revolutionize chip design, we spoke with Heather Gorr, senior product manager for MathWorks’ MATLAB platform.

How is AI currently being used to design the next generation of chips?

Heather Gorr: AI is such an important technology because it’s involved in most parts of the cycle, including the design and manufacturing process. There’s a lot of important applications here, even in the general process engineering where we want to optimize things. I think defect detection is a big one at all phases of the process, especially in manufacturing. But even thinking ahead in the design process, [AI now plays a significant role] when you’re designing the light and the sensors and all the different components. There’s a lot of anomaly detection and fault mitigation that you really want to consider.

Then, thinking about the logistical modeling that you see in any industry, there is always planned downtime that you want to mitigate; but you also end up having unplanned downtime. So, looking back at that historical data of when you’ve had those moments where maybe it took a bit longer than expected to manufacture something, you can take a look at all of that data and use AI to try to identify the proximate cause or to see something that might jump out even in the processing and design phases. We think of AI oftentimes as a predictive tool, or as a robot doing something, but a lot of times you get a lot of insight from the data through AI.

What are the benefits of using AI for chip design?

Gorr: Historically, we’ve seen a lot of physics-based modeling, which is a very intensive process. We want to do a reduced order model, where instead of solving such a computationally expensive and extensive model, we can do something a little cheaper. You could create a surrogate model, so to speak, of that physics-based model, use the data, and then do your parameter sweeps, your optimizations, your Monte Carlo simulations using the surrogate model. That takes a lot less time computationally than solving the physics-based equations directly. So, we’re seeing that benefit in many ways, including the efficiency and economy that are the results of iterating quickly on the experiments and the simulations that will really help in the design.

So it’s like having a digital twin in a sense?

Gorr: Exactly. That’s pretty much what people are doing, where you have the physical system model and the experimental data. Then, in conjunction, you have this other model that you could tweak and tune and try different parameters and experiments that let sweep through all of those different situations and come up with a better design in the end.

So, it’s going to be more efficient and, as you said, cheaper?

Gorr: Yeah, definitely. Especially in the experimentation and design phases, where you’re trying different things. That’s obviously going to yield dramatic cost savings if you’re actually manufacturing and producing [the chips]. You want to simulate, test, experiment as much as possible without making something using the actual process engineering.

We’ve talked about the benefits. How about the drawbacks?

Gorr: The [AI-based experimental models] tend to not be as accurate as physics-based models. Of course, that’s why you do many simulations and parameter sweeps. But that’s also the benefit of having that digital twin, where you can keep that in mind—it’s not going to be as accurate as that precise model that we’ve developed over the years.

Both chip design and manufacturing are system intensive; you have to consider every little part. And that can be really challenging. It’s a case where you might have models to predict something and different parts of it, but you still need to bring it all together.

One of the other things to think about too is that you need the data to build the models. You have to incorporate data from all sorts of different sensors and different sorts of teams, and so that heightens the challenge.

How can engineers use AI to better prepare and extract insights from hardware or sensor data?

Gorr: We always think about using AI to predict something or do some robot task, but you can use AI to come up with patterns and pick out things you might not have noticed before on your own. People will use AI when they have high-frequency data coming from many different sensors, and a lot of times it’s useful to explore the frequency domain and things like data synchronization or resampling. Those can be really challenging if you’re not sure where to start.

One of the things I would say is, use the tools that are available. There’s a vast community of people working on these things, and you can find lots of examples [of applications and techniques] on GitHub or MATLAB Central, where people have shared nice examples, even little apps they’ve created. I think many of us are buried in data and just not sure what to do with it, so definitely take advantage of what’s already out there in the community. You can explore and see what makes sense to you, and bring in that balance of domain knowledge and the insight you get from the tools and AI.

What should engineers and designers consider when using AI for chip design?

Gorr: Think through what problems you’re trying to solve or what insights you might hope to find, and try to be clear about that. Consider all of the different components, and document and test each of those different parts. Consider all of the people involved, and explain and hand off in a way that is sensible for the whole team.

How do you think AI will affect chip designers’ jobs?

Gorr: It’s going to free up a lot of human capital for more advanced tasks. We can use AI to reduce waste, to optimize the materials, to optimize the design, but then you still have that human involved whenever it comes to decision-making. I think it’s a great example of people and technology working hand in hand. It’s also an industry where all people involved—even on the manufacturing floor—need to have some level of understanding of what’s happening, so this is a great industry for advancing AI because of how we test things and how we think about them before we put them on the chip.

How do you envision the future of AI and chip design?

Gorr: It’s very much dependent on that human element—involving people in the process and having that interpretable model. We can do many things with the mathematical minutiae of modeling, but it comes down to how people are using it, how everybody in the process is understanding and applying it. Communication and involvement of people of all skill levels in the process are going to be really important. We’re going to see less of those superprecise predictions and more transparency of information, sharing, and that digital twin—not only using AI but also using our human knowledge and all of the work that many people have done over the years.

Rina Diane Caballar is a writer covering tech and its intersections with science, society, and the environment. An IEEE Spectrum contributing editor, she's a former software engineer based in New Zealand.

#3325. 10 Google Privacy Hacks Everyone Should Know

Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address. In fact, it has unlimited addresses, but you need a hack to utilize them. When you're signing up for a new service, you can add another word to your email address, as well as the "+" symbol, to create an alias. For example, if your email is "[email protected]," and you're signing up for an Amazon account, you can use "[email protected]" as your email address. The email will still end up in your main inbox, as if you simply used [email protected]. Not only can this trick turn one Gmail address into an unlimited number of addresses, but it also helps you identify who sold your email address to spammers, because those emails will have the alias in the "To" field.

Gmail's web view has a crucial security feature that lets you view session logs. This feature is inexplicably buried at the bottom of the inbox, and the font size is tiny, so it's easy to miss. To find it, log in to Gmail on the web, and scroll to the bottom of your inbox. Click the Details button in the bottom-right corner, below "Last account activity." This will show you a pop-up that lists the devices, apps, and locations you've recently logged in from. This makes it easy to see if there's been any suspicious activity in your Google account, and you can click the Security Checkup link in the pop-up to review this data. Just note that if you use a VPN or a service like iCloud Private Relay, you might not recognize your own device's location. To check if unwanted apps have access to your Google account, you can visit this settings page.

Google wants to show you personalized search results, which initially feels very helpful, but it also ends up trapping you in an algorithmic bubble. The best way to break out of your search bubble is to periodically use other search engines, but if you wish to stick to Google, you can disable personalized search recommendations in Google Search and the Play Store on Android. Go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized Recommendations and Play Personalization.

Google tracks your web and app activity by default, which includes your search history, voice data (if you use the speak-to-search feature), and activity from sites, apps, and devices that use Google services. However, associated information, such as your location data, is also saved to your Google profile, which you might not assume gets included in "Web & app activity." Fortunately, you can disable this tracking by going to this settings page, scrolling down to "Web & App Activity," and turning off all options in this section.

Google's Timeline feature saves your location in Google Maps to create a map of places you've visited. This is useful if you want to keep track of your recent stops; however, Google can use Timeline data to help businesses see how effective their ads were, or how likely you are to visit nearby stores. Its confirmation page confirms this: "Depending on your settings, activity saved as history in your Google Account, including ad interactions, may also be connected to Timeline data to help nearby businesses estimate the likelihood that people will visit their stores. No personal information is shared with businesses."

Timeline isn't enabled by default, but in case you enabled it a while ago, and are no longer using it, you can turn it off by going to this settings page. Click Turn off, and delete your activity to remove Timeline data from your Google account.

You can't fully escape Google's ads or tracking, but you can disable personalized ads to stop the company from using your account data to show ads. To do this, go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized ads.

While Google claims that it isn't using your emails to train AI, the company does offer AI features that make your emails feel more robotic than human. One of these is "Smart Reply," which offers email reply suggestions such as "Got it. See you soon." I can type that on my own, and I feel uncomfortable with Gmail analyzing the contents of my emails and replies to offer suggestions that I wouldn't use anyway. You can disable this by going to Gmail Settings > General, or by visiting this settings page. Scroll down to "Smart features," and turn off the checkbox next to it. This will disable Smart Compose, Smart Reply, suggestions for pending replies and follow-ups, spelling, grammar, and autocorrect.

A physical security key is a great security upgrade. It's a physical barrier that prevents most ways to hack into your account remotely. Even if someone discovers your email ID and password, and has access to your two-factor authentication code, they won't get in without physical access to that key. You can check out Google's support page for physical security keys for more information on compatibility and setting up your security keys.

Google uses data from Gmail and Google Drive to target ads, which means that your emails, files, and photos could be used for monetization. To stop this, you'll need to disable Personal Intelligence. To turn it off, visit this settings page, and click Turn off Personal Intelligence.
